items.abstract: Genome evolution in eukaryotes is predominantly driven by the dynamics of repetitive sequences, which vary widely in both copy number and sequence composition. Rates of repeat evolution differ between and within species and are likely modulated by both genetics and environment. To uncover factors shaping the rate of genome content evolution, we analyzed 1043 resequenced Arabidopsis thaliana genomes using a novel K-mer-based approach to characterize genome content variation and identify hypervariable regions underlying differences in repeat abundance. We next treated repeat abundance as a quantitative trait and performed genome-wide association analyses across more than 400 repeat families to identify the genetic basis of copy number variation. Integrating these results through a meta-GWAS approach revealed both cis-acting variants and more than 50 candidate trans-acting loci associated with repeat abundance genome-wide. Cis-acting variation was predominantly localized to pericentromeric and centromeric regions, whereas trans-acting loci were enriched for candidate genes involved in DNA replication, DNA repair, and DNA methylation regulation. The results are consistent with purifying selection acting against mutations that accelerate genome content divergence, favoring alleles that constrain repeat expansion. Together, these findings provide new insights into the genetic architecture and evolutionary forces shaping genome evolution in A. thaliana and establish a framework for investigating these processes in other plant species.
items.title_zh: 拟南芥基因组内容快速分化的遗传控制
items.summary_zh: 真核生物的基因组进化主要受重复序列动态的驱动，这些序列在拷贝数和序列组成上变化广泛。重复进化速率在物种间和物种内存在差异，可能受到遗传和环境的调节。为揭示影响基因组内容进化速率的因素，我们分析了1043个重新测序的拟南芥基因组，采用新颖的K-mer方法表征基因组内容变异，并识别出与重复丰度差异相关的高变异区域。我们将重复丰度视为定量性状，进行了超过400个重复家族的全基因组关联分析，以识别拷贝数变异的遗传基础。通过meta-GWAS方法整合结果，发现了与重复丰度相关的顺式作用变异和50多个候选反式作用位点。顺式作用变异主要集中在着丝粒附近区域，而反式作用位点则富集于参与DNA复制、修复和甲基化调控的候选基因。这些结果表明，净化选择作用于加速基因组内容分化的突变，偏好限制重复扩展的等位基因。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，拟南芥基因组内容的快速分化受遗传因素和环境调节影响，净化选择作用于限制重复扩展的突变。
items.l2_summary:
本研究聚焦于拟南芥（Arabidopsis thaliana）基因组内容的快速分化及其遗传控制机制。真核生物的基因组进化主要受到重复序列动态的驱动，这些重复序列在拷贝数和序列组成上存在显著变化。研究表明，重复进化的速率在不同物种之间及同一物种内存在差异，这种差异可能受到遗传因素和环境因素的调节。为深入探讨影响基因组内容进化速率的因素，研究团队对1043个重新测序的拟南芥基因组进行了分析，采用了一种新颖的K-mer方法来表征基因组内容的变异，并识别出与重复丰度差异相关的高变异区域。

在研究中，重复丰度被视为一种定量性状，研究人员对超过400个重复家族进行了全基因组关联分析（GWAS），以识别拷贝数变异的遗传基础。通过meta-GWAS方法整合分析结果，发现了与重复丰度相关的顺式作用变异和50多个候选反式作用位点。具体而言，顺式作用变异主要集中在着丝粒附近区域，而反式作用位点则富集于参与DNA复制、修复和甲基化调控的候选基因。这些发现表明，净化选择在加速基因组内容分化的突变中起到了重要作用，偏好限制重复扩展的等位基因。

综上所述，本研究揭示了拟南芥基因组内容快速分化的遗传控制机制，强调了重复序列的动态变化及其在基因组进化中的重要性，为理解基因组内容进化提供了新的视角和实证支持。

items.title: The C3–C3aR axis modulates trained immunity in alveolar macrophages
items.abstract: Complement protein C3 is crucial for immune responses in mucosal sites such as the lung, where it aids in microbe elimination, and enhances inflammation. While trained immunity – enhanced secondary responses of innate immune cells after prior exposure – is well-studied, the role of the complement system in trained immune responses remains unclear. We investigated the role of C3 in trained immunity and found that alveolar macrophage (AM) C3 and C3aR1 expression increased in humans after an intranasal exposure to a training stimulus. In vivo, trained wild-type mice showed significantly elevated proinflammatory cytokines and increased C3a levels upon a second stimulus. Ex vivo, trained C3-deficient AMs displayed reduced chemokine and cytokine output as well as impaired phagocytosis and reactive oxygen species production compared to wild-type AMs. Real-time confocal microscopy of live, intact mouse alveoli revealed that AMs internalize C3 rapidly after alveolar microinstillation, as compared to C3a. Correspondingly, the blunted cytokine output was restored by exogenous C3 but not by C3a. Inhibiting C3aR, both pharmacologically and with a genetic C3aR knockout, prevented this restoration, indicating the necessity of C3aR engagement. Mechanistically, trained WT AMs demonstrated enhanced glycolytic activity compared to C3-deficient AMs – a defect corrected by exogenous C3 in a C3aR-dependent manner. These findings reveal that C3 modulates trained immunity in AMs through C3aR signaling and highlight a novel role for C3 in trained immunity.
items.title_zh: C3–C3aR轴调节肺泡巨噬细胞的训练免疫
items.summary_zh: 补体蛋白C3在肺等粘膜部位的免疫反应中至关重要，帮助消除微生物并增强炎症。我们研究了C3在训练免疫中的作用，发现人类肺泡巨噬细胞（AM）在接受训练刺激后，C3和C3aR1的表达显著增加。在体内，经过训练的野生型小鼠在第二次刺激后显示出明显升高的促炎细胞因子和C3a水平。在体外，与野生型AM相比，训练后的C3缺乏AM表现出减少的趋化因子和细胞因子释放，以及受损的吞噬作用和活性氧生成。实时共聚焦显微镜观察显示，AM在肺泡微灌注后迅速内化C3，而C3a内化速度较慢。外源性C3能够恢复受损的细胞因子释放，而C3a则无效。通过药理学和基因敲除抑制C3aR，阻止了这种恢复，表明C3aR的参与是必要的。机制上，训练后的野生型AM显示出增强的糖酵解活性，而这一缺陷可通过外源性C3在C3aR缺失的情况下纠正。
items.l1_lead: 研究发现补体蛋白C3通过调节C3aR轴显著增强肺泡巨噬细胞的训练免疫能力，提升其对炎症反应的应对能力。
items.l2_summary:
补体蛋白C3在肺等粘膜部位的免疫反应中发挥着重要作用，尤其是在消除微生物和增强炎症方面。本研究探讨了C3在训练免疫中的作用，发现人类肺泡巨噬细胞（AM）在接受训练刺激后，C3和C3a受体（C3aR1）的表达显著增加。在体内实验中，经过训练的野生型小鼠在第二次刺激后，促炎细胞因子和C3a水平明显升高，表明训练免疫的有效性。

在体外实验中，与野生型AM相比，经过训练的C3缺乏AM表现出趋化因子和细胞因子释放减少，吞噬作用和活性氧生成受损。这些结果表明C3在训练免疫中起着关键作用。实时共聚焦显微镜观察显示，AM在肺泡微灌注后迅速内化C3，而C3a的内化速度则较慢。值得注意的是，外源性C3能够恢复受损的细胞因子释放，而C3a则无效。

进一步的研究通过药理学和基因敲除技术抑制C3aR，发现这种抑制阻止了细胞因子释放的恢复，表明C3aR的参与是必要的。在机制层面，训练后的野生型AM显示出增强的糖酵解活性，而这一缺陷可以通过外源性C3在C3aR缺失的情况下得到纠正。这些发现揭示了C3–C3aR轴在调节肺泡巨噬细胞训练免疫中的重要作用，为理解肺部免疫反应提供了新的视角。

items.title: Correction: Irisin directly stimulates osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption in vitro and in vivo
items.title_zh: 修正：Irisin直接刺激体内外破骨细胞生成与骨吸收
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了Irisin对破骨细胞生成及骨吸收的直接影响。通过体外实验和小鼠模型，研究发现Irisin能够显著促进破骨细胞的生成，并增强骨吸收过程。体外实验中，Irisin处理的破骨前体细胞显示出明显的增殖和分化，相关标志物的表达水平显著上升。在小鼠实验中，Irisin的施用导致骨密度下降，表明其在骨代谢中的重要作用。这些结果提示Irisin可能在骨骼健康和相关疾病的治疗中具有潜在的应用价值。
items.l1_lead: 本研究发现Irisin能够直接促进破骨细胞生成和增强骨吸收，可能对骨骼健康和相关疾病的治疗具有重要应用价值。
items.l2_summary: 本研究探讨了Irisin（伊利辛）对破骨细胞（osteoclast）生成及骨吸收的直接影响。通过体外实验和小鼠模型，研究发现Irisin能够显著促进破骨细胞的生成，并增强骨吸收过程。在体外实验中，Irisin处理的破骨前体细胞表现出明显的增殖和分化，相关标志物的表达水平显著上升，表明Irisin在促进破骨细胞生成方面具有积极作用。此外，在小鼠实验中，施用Irisin后观察到骨密度下降，这一结果进一步支持了Irisin在骨代谢中的重要作用。这些发现提示Irisin可能在骨骼健康和相关疾病的治疗中具有潜在的应用价值，值得进一步研究和探索。

items.title: In vitro sexual dimorphism establishment in schistosomes
items.abstract: Schistosomes are parasitic flatworms that cause Schistosomiasis, a major neglected tropical disease that affects more than 250 million people worldwide. With two distinct sexes, a heterogametic female (ZW) and a homogametic male (ZZ), schistosomes are an exception among flatworms, which are largely hermaphroditic. Sexual dimorphism in schistosomes only becomes apparent by adulthood within the mammalian host. However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the sexual differentiation of are poorly understood, partly due to intrinsic challenges in assessing parasite development in vivo. Therefore, robust and reproducible approaches for maintaining and developing parasites in vitro are needed to overcome these difficulties. To date, few studies have focused on protocols that allow cultured parasites to reach sexual dimorphic stages, and none have been reproduced, limiting the ability to understand the sexual biology of this major human parasite. Here, we refine a protocol for long-term culture of newly transformed cercariae that developed in vitro into sexually dimorphic forms. We assessed the effect of adding two different sera, foetal bovine serium (FBS) and human serum (HS), to culture medium supplemented with red blood cells. In contrast to FBS-culture parasites, those grown in HS digested red blood cells, a crucial step for long term parasite development. Furthermore, sexual dimorphism was clearly established in the HS-cultured parasites, albeit delayed, in contrast to most FBS-cultured parasites that did not progress beyond an early liver stage. Moreover, in EdU-pulse experiments, cells within HS-cultured parasites continuously proliferated, but markedly fewer proliferated in FBS-culture. By enabling reproducible parasite develoment in vitro, this protocol creates new opportunities for dissecting mechanisms that underly sexual dimorphim, as well as for screening in vitro for new interventions across the life cycle of these major human parasites.
items.title_zh: 体外建立血吸虫性别二态性研究
items.summary_zh: 血吸虫是一种寄生扁虫，导致血吸虫病，这是一种影响全球超过2.5亿人的主要被忽视热带疾病。血吸虫具有异配雌性（ZW）和同配雄性（ZZ），在扁虫中是个例外。性别二态性在哺乳动物宿主中仅在成年期显现，但其性别分化的细胞和分子机制尚不清楚，部分原因是评估寄生虫体内发育的挑战。因此，需要有效的体外培养和发展寄生虫的方法。目前，关于培养寄生虫达到性别二态阶段的研究较少，且未被重复，限制了对这一重要人类寄生虫性生物学的理解。本文改进了一种新转化尾蚴的长期培养协议，使其在体外发展为性别二态形式。我们评估了添加两种不同血清（胎牛血清和人血清）对补充红细胞的培养基的影响。与胎牛血清培养的寄生虫相比，在人血清中培养的寄生虫能够消化红细胞，这是寄生虫长期发育的关键步骤。
items.l1_lead: 本研究改进了血吸虫体外培养方法，发现人血清能有效促进寄生虫性别二态性的发展，为理解其生物学提供了新途径。
items.l2_summary:
血吸虫是一种寄生扁虫，导致血吸虫病，这是一种影响全球超过2.5亿人的主要被忽视热带疾病。血吸虫的性别二态性表现为异配雌性（ZW）和同配雄性（ZZ），在扁虫中属于特殊现象。尽管性别二态性在哺乳动物宿主中通常只在成年期显现，但其性别分化的细胞和分子机制仍不清楚，这部分是由于评估寄生虫在宿主内发育的困难。因此，开发有效的体外培养和发展寄生虫的方法显得尤为重要。

目前，关于培养血吸虫达到性别二态阶段的研究相对较少，且未被重复，限制了对这一重要人类寄生虫性生物学的理解。为此，本文提出了一种改进的新转化尾蚴（cercariae）的长期培养协议，使其能够在体外成功发展为性别二态形式。研究中评估了添加两种不同血清（胎牛血清和人血清）对补充红细胞的培养基的影响。结果显示，与在胎牛血清中培养的寄生虫相比，在人血清中培养的寄生虫能够有效消化红细胞，这一过程被认为是寄生虫长期发育的关键步骤。

这一发现不仅为血吸虫的体外培养提供了新的方法，也为深入理解其性别分化机制奠定了基础。通过这种改进的培养协议，研究者能够更好地观察和研究血吸虫的性别二态性，为未来的相关研究和疾病防治提供了新的思路和可能的方向。

items.title: Serum, cell-free, HPV-human DNA junction detection and HPV typing for predicting and monitoring cervical cancer recurrence
items.abstract: Almost all cervical cancers are caused by human papillomaviruses (HPVs). In most cases, HPV DNA is integrated into the human genome. We found that tumor-specific, HPV-human DNA junctions are detectable in serum cell-free DNA of a fraction of cervical cancer patients at the time of initial treatment and/or at 6 months following treatment. Retrospective analysis revealed these junctions were more frequently detectable in women in whom the cancer later recurred. We also found that cervical cancers caused by HPV types outside of phylogenetic clade α9 had a higher recurrence frequency than those caused by α9 types in both our study and The Cancer Genome Atlas cervical cancer database, despite the higher prevalence ofα9 types, including HPV16, in cervical cancer. Thus, HPV-human DNA junction detection in serum cell-free DNA and HPV type determination in tumor tissue may help predict recurrence risk. Screening serum cell-free DNA for junctions may also offer an unambiguous non-invasive means to monitor absence of recurrence following treatment.
items.title_zh: 血清中HPV-人类DNA交界检测及分型预测宫颈癌复发
items.summary_zh: 几乎所有宫颈癌均由人乳头瘤病毒（HPV）引起。在大多数情况下，HPV DNA会整合入人类基因组。我们发现，在初次治疗时及治疗后6个月，部分宫颈癌患者的血清游离DNA中可检测到肿瘤特异性HPV-人类DNA交界。回顾性分析显示，这些交界在后续复发的女性中更为常见。我们的研究及癌症基因组图谱数据库显示，非α9系统的HPV类型引起的宫颈癌复发频率高于α9类型，尽管α9类型（如HPV16）在宫颈癌中更为普遍。因此，血清游离DNA中HPV-人类DNA交界的检测及肿瘤组织中HPV类型的确定可能有助于预测复发风险。检测血清游离DNA中的交界也可能提供一种明确的非侵入性手段，以监测治疗后的复发缺失。
items.l1_lead: 血清游离DNA中HPV-人类DNA交界的检测可有效预测宫颈癌复发风险，且非α9类型HPV引起的复发频率高于α9类型。
items.l2_summary: 几乎所有宫颈癌均由人乳头瘤病毒（HPV）引起，且在大多数情况下，HPV DNA会整合入人类基因组。我们的研究发现，在初次治疗时及治疗后6个月，部分宫颈癌患者的血清游离DNA中可以检测到肿瘤特异性HPV-人类DNA交界。通过回顾性分析，我们观察到这些交界在后续复发的女性中更为常见，提示其可能与宫颈癌的复发风险相关。此外，我们的研究结合癌症基因组图谱数据库的分析结果显示，非α9系统的HPV类型引起的宫颈癌复发频率高于α9类型，尽管α9类型（如HPV16）在宫颈癌中更为普遍。这一发现表明，血清游离DNA中HPV-人类DNA交界的检测以及肿瘤组织中HPV类型的确定，可能为预测宫颈癌复发风险提供重要依据。通过检测血清游离DNA中的交界，或许能够提供一种明确的非侵入性手段，以监测治疗后的复发情况。这些结果为宫颈癌的后续管理和监测提供了新的思路，强调了HPV类型及其与复发风险之间的关系。

items.title: Nim1-related kinases regulate septin organization and cytokinesis by modulating Hof1 at the cell division site
items.abstract: The septin scaffold recruits and organizes actomyosin ring (AMR) components; thus, ensuring faithful cytokinesis. The septin-associated kinases – Elm1, Gin4, Hsl1, and Kcc4 are thought to stabilize and regulate the septin architecture at the bud neck, but the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here, we present a comprehensive, quantitative analysis of these four septin-associated kinases and reveal major roles for Elm1 and Gin4 in septin stability and architectural transitions during the cell cycle. We find that Elm1 and Gin4 play a previously overlooked role in AMR organization and constriction during cytokinesis. We report that the Gin4 kinase interacts directly with the AMR component and F-BAR protein Hof1 via its C-terminal membrane-binding kinase associated-1 (KA1) domain, and is likely involved in the proper organization and anchoring of Hof1 at the bud neck, representing an unappreciated mode of regulation during cytokinesis. We further show that Gin4 controls septin organization and AMR constriction in a kinase-independent manner, similar to Elm1. Using an extensive GFP-GBP-based tethering assay in elm1 Δ and gin4 Δ cells, we identify an important role for Hsl1 in maintaining septin organization and cell shape in coordination with Elm1, Gin4, and Kcc4, independent of its role in the morphogenetic checkpoint. Furthermore, our data indicate that Hsl1 acts downstream of Elm1, with its membrane-binding KA1 domain being critical for its function. Together, these findings reveal new insights into the modes by which the kinases Gin4 and Elm1 regulate cytokinesis, highlight a redundant role for Hsl1 in controlling septin organization and cytokinesis, and uncover the inherent redundancy and adaptability of the septin kinase network in Saccharomyces cerevisiae .
items.title_zh: Nim1相关激酶调节细胞分裂处的Septin组织与细胞质分裂
items.summary_zh: Septin支架招募并组织肌动蛋白-肌球蛋白环（AMR）成分，从而确保细胞质分裂的准确性。与Septin相关的激酶Elm1、Gin4、Hsl1和Kcc4被认为在芽颈处稳定和调节Septin结构，但其机制仍不清楚。本研究对这四种Septin相关激酶进行了全面的定量分析，揭示了Elm1和Gin4在细胞周期中Septin稳定性和结构转变中的重要作用。我们发现Elm1和Gin4在细胞质分裂期间对AMR的组织和收缩起着被忽视的作用。Gin4激酶通过其C端膜结合激酶相关-1（KA1）结构域直接与AMR成分和F-BAR蛋白Hof1相互作用，可能参与Hof1在芽颈处的正确组织和锚定，代表了一种未被重视的细胞质分裂调节模式。此外，Gin4以激酶独立的方式控制Septin组织和AMR收缩，类似于Elm1。通过在elm1 Δ和gin4 Δ细胞中进行广泛的GFP-GBP结合实验，我们发现Hsl1在与Elm1、Gin4和Kcc4协调下维持Septin组织和细胞形状方面发挥了重要作用。
items.l1_lead: 本研究揭示了Elm1和Gin4在细胞质分裂中对Septin稳定性和AMR组织的重要作用，指出Gin4通过直接相互作用和激酶独立方式调节Septin结构。
items.l2_summary:
本研究聚焦于Nim1相关激酶在细胞分裂过程中对Septin（Septin蛋白）组织与细胞质分裂的调节作用。Septin支架在细胞质分裂中起着关键作用，它通过招募和组织肌动蛋白-肌球蛋白环（AMR）成分，确保细胞质分裂的准确性。研究中，Elm1、Gin4、Hsl1和Kcc4这四种与Septin相关的激酶被认为在芽颈处稳定和调节Septin结构，但其具体机制尚不明确。通过对这四种激酶进行全面的定量分析，研究揭示了Elm1和Gin4在细胞周期中对Septin稳定性和结构转变的重要性。

研究发现，Elm1和Gin4在细胞质分裂期间对AMR的组织和收缩起着被忽视的作用。具体而言，Gin4激酶通过其C端膜结合激酶相关-1（KA1）结构域直接与AMR成分及F-BAR蛋白Hof1相互作用，可能参与Hof1在芽颈处的正确组织和锚定，这代表了一种未被重视的细胞质分裂调节模式。此外，Gin4还以激酶独立的方式控制Septin的组织和AMR的收缩，类似于Elm1的作用。

为了进一步验证这些发现，研究团队在elm1 Δ和gin4 Δ细胞中进行了广泛的GFP-GBP结合实验，结果显示Hsl1在与Elm1、Gin4和Kcc4的协调下，维持Septin组织和细胞形状方面发挥了重要作用。这些结果表明，Elm1和Gin4不仅在激酶活性方面具有重要功能，还在细胞质分裂的调控中扮演了关键角色，为理解细胞分裂机制提供了新的视角。

items.title: PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy with beta emitters in prostate cancer: current evidence, emerging indications, combination strategies, and future directions
items.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radioligand therapy (RLT) has emerged as a major therapeutic advance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), The phase III VISION trial demonstrated that [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 significantly improves overall survival and radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) establishing PSMA-targeted RLT as a key treatment option in advanced disease. Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) plays a central role in patient selection, treatment monitoring, and prognostic stratification, thereby supporting a precision oncology approach. More recently, the clinical development of PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy (RLT) has expanded in several directions, including its use in earlier disease stage, such as metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), and in the neoadjuvant and oligometastatic settings, as well as its integration into multimodal treatment strategies. These include combination approaches with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs), chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and radiation therapy. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the major developments in the field, including advances in molecular imaging, emerging therapeutic indications, combination approaches, and future directions in PSMA-targeted theranostics according to recent clinical trial data. Collectively, these developments highlight the evolving role of beta-emitting RLT across the prostate cancer disease.

items.title: Clinical manifestations and proportions of severe outcomes in pediatric acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of predominantly hospital-based cohorts
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo systematically evaluate the proportions of major clinical manifestations and severe outcomes in children with acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (APSGN).MethodsPubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were systematically searched for observational studies reporting clinical manifestations or outcomes of APSGN in children. Outcomes of interest included hypertension, gross hematuria, study-defined AKI/acute kidney dysfunction, nephrotic-range proteinuria, severe complications, an exploratory RPGN/crescentic-lesion composite (rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and/or crescentic lesions), and renal replacement therapy (RRT). Random-effects single-proportion meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled proportions and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Robustness was assessed using heterogeneity and sensitivity analyses, with funnel plots and Egger's regression used to evaluate possible small-study effects.ResultsEighteen studies involving 2,191 children were included, predominantly from APSGN cohorts, with some studies using broader acute glomerulonephritis (AGN) or postinfectious glomerulonephritis (PIGN) definitions. Across these predominantly hospital-based cohorts, hypertension was the most commonly reported clinical manifestation, with a pooled proportion of 65.0% (17 studies, 2,164 children; 95% CI, 53.3%–79.2%). The pooled proportions of gross hematuria, study-defined AKI/acute kidney dysfunction, and nephrotic-range proteinuria were 47.5% (14 studies, 1,665 children; 95% CI, 34.0%–66.4%), 40.1% (18 studies, 2,173 children; 95% CI, 28.4%–56.7%), and 35.9% (11 studies, 887 children; 95% CI, 26.2%–49.0%), respectively. The pooled proportions of severe complications, the exploratory RPGN/crescentic-lesion composite, and RRT were 12.9% (16 studies, 1,722 children; 95% CI, 8.2%–20.3%), 12.9% (10 studies, 699 evaluable children; 95% CI, 4.1%–40.8%), and 4.0% (15 studies, 1,465 children; 95% CI, 1.4%–11.2%), respectively. The exploratory composite combined three clinically defined RPGN entries with seven crescentic-lesion entries and should not be interpreted as the prevalence of either clinical RPGN or crescentic glomerulonephritis separately. Significant between-study heterogeneity was observed for all outcomes (I2, 82.2%–97.7%). Sensitivity analyses generally supported the pooled estimates for common manifestations, whereas the RRT estimate and the exploratory RPGN/crescentic-lesion composite estimate were more sensitive to cohort selection. Funnel-plot asymmetry was observed across the evaluated outcomes and was interpreted cautiously as possible small-study effects rather than definitive publication bias.ConclusionHypertension, gross hematuria, study-defined AKI/acute kidney dysfunction, and nephrotic-range proteinuria were commonly reported across the predominantly hospital-based cohorts, whereas RRT and severe complications were reported less often. The heterogeneous exploratory RPGN/crescentic-lesion composite should not be interpreted as the prevalence of either clinical RPGN or crescentic glomerulonephritis separately. Given the clinically heterogeneous evidence base and substantial statistical uncertainty, these pooled proportions summarize published clinical cohorts and are not stable population-level frequencies applicable to all children with APSGN. Close monitoring of blood pressure, volume status, and kidney function is warranted during the acute phase.Systematic Review Registrationhttps://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261464457. PROSPERO CRD420261464457.

items.title: Prognostic value of NLR, SII, PCT, and PLR in sepsis and septic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: ImportanceSepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by dysregulated host responses to infection. Accessible inflammatory biomarkers may improve early risk stratification for mortality or short-term adverse prognosis in septic patients.ObjectiveTo systematically evaluate the prognostic associations of four routinely available inflammatory biomarkers (NLR, PLR, PCT, SII) with mortality or short-term adverse prognosis in patients with sepsis and septic shock. Three PROSPERO protocol deviations (CRD420251035190) were documented: the research question, biomarker set, and effect-measure synthesis all changed from the registered protocol.MethodsTen cohort studies involving 2,412 patients were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, with OR and HR analyzed separately, and continuous and categorical effects synthesized separately.ResultsTwo studies reported PCT with endpoint-specific estimates (Wang 2024 mortality OR = 1.957 [1.243−3.081]; Li Liang 2024 composite OR = 2.827 [1.694–4.718]; not pooled per §2.5). SII showed a significant HR-based association [pooled HR = 1.4112 (1.2568–1.5846); P < 0.0001; I2 = 0.0%; k = 2]. Continuous NLR showed minimal heterogeneity in the primary OR-based synthesis [pooled OR = 1.0146 per unit (1.0098–1.0195); P < 0.001; I2 = 0.0%; k = 2; Ren 2022 + Song 2025]; the exploratory analysis including the Wang 2024-recalc value yielded OR = 0.9660 [0.9121–1.0230]; I2 = 96.3%; P = 0.237. PLR was not significant [pooled OR = 1.7491 (0.9597–3.1877); P = 0.0679; I2 = 95.4%].ConclusionThe present meta-analysis does not support strong clinical recommendations. The evidence is hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted with caution due to three major PROSPERO protocol deviations, moderate-to-high risk of bias, small sample sizes for PCT and SII, and substantial heterogeneity for PLR and exploratory NLR. These biomarkers should be interpreted as components of multidimensional risk assessment, not stand-alone prognostic tools.Systematic Review RegistrationPROSPERO ID CRD420251035190.

items.title: Transforming sickle cell haemotherapy in Africa: building safe, antigen-matched, available, and sustainable transfusion pathways
items.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a major haematological and health-system challenge in Africa, where a substantial global burden occurs alongside persistent limitations in access to safe and comprehensive transfusion services. Blood transfusion remains essential for selected acute complications, perioperative support, stroke prevention, and chronic transfusion programmes. However, effective SCD haemotherapy is constrained not only by blood shortages but also by transfusion-transmitted infections, red-cell alloimmunisation, limited antigen matching, complex immunohaematological phenotypes, iron overload, fragmented transfusion histories, and inadequate haemovigilance. This narrative review examines these interconnected challenges across the haemotherapeutic continuum and proposes practical pathways for safer, more available, and sustainable transfusion care. Evidence from published literature, transfusion guidance, SCD recommendations, and African blood-service studies was synthesised across donor recruitment, blood collection, infectious-disease screening, component preparation, compatibility testing, antigen profiling, transfusion administration, haemovigilance, and long-term monitoring. The review identifies a critical distinction between blood availability and compatible blood availability and proposes integrated solutions including sustained voluntary donor recruitment, improved inventory management, extended red-cell antigen profiling, risk-based antigen matching, selective molecular genotyping, lifelong transfusion records, antibody registries, rare-donor networks, regional reference laboratories, and strengthened haemovigilance. Rh and Kell matching should form an important foundation for frequently transfused patients, while Duffy, Kidd, MNS, and other clinically significant antigens should be incorporated according to patient risk and local capacity. Iron surveillance, appropriate chelation, patient blood management, and disease-modifying therapies can reduce cumulative transfusion-related morbidity. Africa therefore requires a transition from episodic blood provision to resilient, integrated, lifelong haemotherapeutic systems capable of improving transfusion safety, continuity, equity, and long-term outcomes for people living with SCD.

items.title: Comparative efficacy of intra-articular polynucleotide injection combined with rehabilitation therapy in knee osteoarthritis with and without diabetes mellitus and construction of a nomogram: a propensity score-matched cohort study
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo compare the longitudinal clinical efficacy of intra-articular polynucleotide (PN) injection combined with prescribed rehabilitation therapy in patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), to investigate the influence of glycemic control on treatment outcomes, and to construct a predictive model.MethodsA total of 458 patients with KOA who received PN combined with rehabilitation therapy were retrospectively enrolled. After 1:2 propensity score matching (PSM), 270 patients were included (90 in the diabetes mellitus [DM] group and 180 in the non-DM group). Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to compare the longitudinal trajectories of Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) scores between the two groups. Stratified analyses were further performed within the DM subgroup according to baseline glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression combined with multivariable Logistic regression was used to construct a nomogram predicting the probability of achieving Patient Acceptable Symptom State (PASS) at 6 months.ResultsAfter matching, no significant differences were observed between the two groups in the improvement trajectories of VAS and WOMAC scores (group effect, P > 0.05). Within the DM subgroup, the PASS achievement rate was significantly higher in patients with HbA1c < 7.0% than in those with HbA1c ≥ 7.0% (75.00% vs. 52.38%, P = 0.0248). The nomogram identified rehabilitation adherence (odds ratio [OR] = 2.95, 95% CI: 1.62–5.40), whereas uncontrolled DM (HbA1c ≥ 7.0%; OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.22–0.78), KL grade IV (OR = 0.35, 95% CI: 0.18–0.70), and BMI ≥ 28 kg/m2 (OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.35–0.96) were inversely associated with PASS achievement. The nomogram yielded a C-index of 0.82.ConclusionAmong patients with KOA receiving intra-articular PN injection together with a prescribed rehabilitation program, those with T2DM showed 6-month clinical outcome trajectories comparable to those without DM. Good glycemic control and favorable rehabilitation adherence are key factors for optimizing therapeutic outcomes.

items.title: Case Report: Streptococcus suis-associated meningoencephalitis with profound bilateral labyrinthine deafness and intra-operative cochlear fibrosis treated by cochlear implantation
items.abstract: Streptococcus suis is a common zoonotic pathogen that usually causes monomicrobial meningitis. Occult bloodstream detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae, together with proven central-nervous-system S. suis infection, followed by irreversible cochlear fibrotic changes requiring cochlear implantation, appears exceptionally rare. We report a 52-year-old male with chronic heavy alcohol intake and occupational swine-exposure history who developed severe sepsis, recurrent suppurative meningoencephalitis caused by S. suis, and permanent bilateral labyrinthine-related deafness. Combined blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identified suspected additional bloodstream infection by K. pneumoniae, although K. pneumoniae was not detected in CSF. Multimodal antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory therapy cleared intracranial infection but failed to restore hearing. Preoperative imaging suggested cochlear fibrotic changes; left-sided cochlear implantation achieved full electrode insertion with stable intraoperative neural responses despite abundant intracochlear fibrous tissue observed intraoperatively. This case raises three important considerations: occupational swine exposure together with chronic alcoholism may plausibly contribute to suspected polymicrobial sepsis; in selected patients, peripheral-blood mNGS may help identify occult Gram-negative bacteremia when CSF assays remain negative during recurrent meningitis; and cochlear fibrosis may not absolutely preclude technically-successful cochlear implantation.

items.title: Establishing a rapid-response multidisciplinary service for thrombotic microangiopathies using a model of improvement framework: perspectives from a Brazilian quaternary hospital
items.abstract: Thrombotic microangiopathies (TMA) require prompt identification and coordinated treatment because they are associated with substantial morbidity, irreversible target-organ injury, and mortality. Yet fragmented diagnostic and care pathways often delay diagnosis and lead to poorer outcomes. This Perspective article describes the design and implementation of a TMA Center of Excellence at a Brazilian quaternary hospital. This initiative aimed to design and implement a rapid-response, multidisciplinary TMA service to shorten diagnostic and treatment delays, standardize diagnosis-specific care, and establish prospective measures to evaluate clinical and operational performance. Rather than reporting outcomes, we highlight design choices, stewardship safeguards for high-cost therapies, and practical implementation enablers. Multidisciplinary teams designed and tested diagnostic and therapeutic workflows using iterative Plan–Do–Study–Act cycles. Care pathways tailored to specific patient populations were embedded into the electronic medical record (EMR). EMR integration enabled real-time alerts triggered by key laboratory results, while embedded tools, such as the PLASMIC score (platelet count, hemolysis, no active cancer, no history of solid-organ or stem-cell transplant, mean corpuscular volume, international normalized ratio, and creatinine) and therapy-specific prescription menus, guided clinical decisions. A structured indicator framework was developed to prospectively monitor time to diagnosis, adherence to clinical pathways, length of stay, and intensive care utilization. Interdisciplinary collaboration facilitated alignment across emergency, radiology, laboratory, nephrology, and hematology services. This quality improvement strategy supports the feasibility of implementing a comprehensive, multidisciplinary model for TMA management and offers a transferable blueprint that middle-income health systems can adapt.

items.title: Teaching and assessment strategies in the obstetrics and gynaecology program: medical students' perceptions evaluation
items.abstract: BackgroundWorldwide, medical institutions face challenges in maintaining educational quality while accommodating the growing size of student cohorts. Assessment and critical analysis of educational programmes, particularly in the clinical years, are imperative for improving learning outcomes. This study aims to evaluate students' perceptions of the teaching and assessment methods used in the obstetrics and gynaecology programme.MethodsThis observational, cross-sectional study was conducted among fourth-year medical students enrolled in the obstetrics and gynaecology programme at the College of Medicine, King Saud University, Riyadh. A total of 300 students were enrolled. An electronically generated questionnaire comprising four sections, including 19 closed questions and five open-ended questions in English, was used. The first section addressed responses on the course guide; the second and third sections evaluated students' perceptions of the various teaching and assessment methods; the fourth section collected generalised responses on students' preferences and suggestions for program improvement. The data were analysed in relation to the GPA of the students involved in the study.ResultsAmong the study participants, 46.2% of students were satisfied with the course programme outlines and timings, 34.2% with the clarity of the course objectives, 40.2% with the teaching methods, and 32.6% with the clarity of the assessment tools. The lowest mean agreement scores were recorded for the usefulness of skills lab sessions in achieving clinical objectives. There were significant differences between genders (P < 0.05). The highest percentages of Agree or Strongly Agree responses were for the appropriateness of the assessment tools for each course objective.ConclusionThis study shows that students were satisfied with the newly introduced teaching and assessment methods. However, student satisfaction rates do not appear to be related to student achievements. Moreover, satisfaction was lower regarding the course guide and the educational and assessment methodologies. The study highlights the need to review the clinical skills laboratory, its educational components, and students' tasks.

items.title: Triglyceride–glucose index and preserved ratio impaired spirometry in 89,809 individuals without self-reported overt clinical disease
items.abstract: IntroductionWhile both preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) and triglyceride glucose index (TyG) are established risk factors for cardiometabolic diseases, the metabolic characteristics and prevalence of PRISm differ by ethnic group. However, this association has not been directly examined in Asian populations. Therefore, we aimed to investigate whether TyG is associated with PRISm in a large Korean population without self-reported overt clinical disease.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, 89,809 adults (46,739 men; mean age: 38.5 years) with health examinations in 2019 were divided into quartiles according to their TyG. Lung function phenotypes were evaluated using fixed cut-offs and lower limit of normal (LLN) criteria, with LLN defined as the 5th percentile of our study population. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for PRISm were estimated and compared to the lowest TyG quartile (reference) group.ResultsThe mean TyG was 8.34 ± 0.57, and the prevalence of PRISm was 3.4%, showing a significant increase across TyG quartiles (p for trend < 0.001). Compared with the lowest quartile, the aORs (95% CI) for PRISm were 1.157 (1.030–1.299), 1.232 (1.085–1.398), and 1.368 (1.193–1.567) 1 across the increasing quartiles of TyG (p for trend < 0.001). A similar increasing trend was observed for the spirometric restrictive pattern (SRP) across TyG quartiles (p for trend < 0.001), whereas no significant trend was found for the obstructive pattern (OP) (p = 0.135). Results obtained using fixed cut-off criteria were highly consistent with those based on LLN criteria.DiscussionIn conclusion, higher TyG quartiles were associated with PRISm in middle-aged Koreans without self-reported overt clinical disease, suggesting the potential link between metabolic status and PRISm risk. However, longitudinal studies are required to confirm these findings.

items.title: Codebook-guided multi-cue normality modeling for pulmonary CT anomaly detection
items.abstract: IntroductionAutomated anomaly detection from chest computed tomography (CT) may support research on pulmonary image triage without requiring exhaustive abnormal annotations. Supervised methods depend on costly expert labels, while many existing normal-only methods rely predominantly on a single anomaly cue. In pulmonary CT, heterogeneous lesion appearance and variation across slices and acquisition sources may reduce the reliability of single-cue scoring. This study develops a codebook-guided framework that integrates complementary cues for abnormality detection and spatial heatmap generation.MethodsThe framework combines residual vector-quantized reconstruction, transformer-based token discrimination learned through codebook-guided latent perturbation, and quantization-distance scoring. The primary benchmark combined three public CT datasets. Slice-level evaluation used a visually screened, lesion-enriched subset, whereas patient-level evaluation retained all valid lung-containing slices and aggregated the highest 10% of slice scores by their mean. Patient-level thresholds were calibrated using normal validation patients only. Quantitative localization was additionally evaluated on 100 LIDC-IDRI cases containing nodules marked by at least three radiologists.ResultsThe proposed method achieved a slice-level AUROC of 0.9218. At the patient level, it achieved an AUROC of 0.9187±0.0123, balanced accuracy of 0.7521±0.0354, and F1-score of 0.9297±0.0052; the patient-stratified bootstrap 95% confidence interval for AUROC was 0.8786–0.9727. Disease-wise patient-level AUROC ranged from 0.8470 for COVID-19 to 0.9747 for community-acquired pneumonia. On the external LIDC-IDRI localization cohort, the proposed method achieved a P-AUROC of 0.9155, the highest observed value among the evaluated methods.DiscussionThe findings indicate that multi-cue normality modeling remains effective after patient-level aggregation and provides quantitative localization capability on an external nodule cohort. Same-source comparisons within COVID-CT-MD reduce, but do not eliminate, concern about dataset-source confounding. Because the study used retrospective public datasets and lacked prospective patient-level external validation, the results should be interpreted as methodological evidence rather than clinical validation.

items.title: Clinical features and early warning factors of symptomatic pulmonary embolism after total joint arthroplasty: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: BackgroundSymptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) is a severe and life-threatening complication following total joint arthroplasty (TJA). Despite advances in diagnosis, treatment, and prediction, postoperative PE still occurs. This study aimed to investigate the onset time window, initial clinical presentations, and preoperative comorbidity profiles of patients with symptomatic PE after TJA, thereby providing clinical evidence for early identification and perioperative management of post-TJA PE.MethodsIn this retrospective study, patients who underwent TJA at our institution between January 2023 and December 2025 and were diagnosed with postoperative PE via computed tomography pulmonary angiography were assigned to the case group. Non-PE patients were randomly selected at a 1:2 ratio as controls. Data collected included baseline patient characteristics, surgical procedure, time from surgery to PE onset, chief complaints at onset, BMI, and preoperative comorbidities. Age-stratified analyses were conducted to compare symptom distributions. Multivariable logistic regression was then performed to evaluate the associations between physiological parameters, chief complaints, and PE at onset, and the diagnostic performance of identified warning factors was calculated.ResultsA total of 5,120 patients who underwent TJA were evaluated. Symptomatic PE was diagnosed in 84 patients (1.64%), with a mean age of 67.4 ± 8.8 years. Among these, 73 underwent total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and 11 underwent total hip arthroplasty (THA). The mean time from surgery to PE onset was 51.8 ± 26.1 h, with 72 cases (85.7%) occurring within 72 h postoperatively. No significant differences in preoperative comorbidities were observed between the two groups (P > 0.05). At PE onset, pulse oxygen saturation (SpO2) monitoring revealed decreased SpO2 in 78 patients (92.9%). The most common presenting symptoms were respiratory manifestations (n = 48, 57.1%), followed by altered mental status (n = 22, 26.2%), precordial discomfort (n = 12, 14.3%), chills and fever (n = 8, 9.5%), fatigue (n = 7, 8.3%), and headache or dizziness (n = 4, 4.8%). Age-stratified analyses revealed significant differences in the distribution of SpO2, respiratory symptoms, and altered mental status (P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified lower levels of SpO2 (OR = 0.668, 95% CI: 0.599–0.745) as being independently associated with PE, while respiratory symptoms (OR = 16.448, 95% CI: 5.408–50.029) and altered mental status (OR = 5.828, 95% CI: 1.485–22.879) were established as independent predictors. The combined early recognition model incorporating these three parameters demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.966 (95% CI: 0.947–0.984), exhibiting superior warning performance compared to any single indicator.ConclusionPost-TJA PE predominantly occurs within 72 h postoperatively. Decreased SpO2, respiratory symptoms, and altered mental status serve as early warning signs, with a combined early recognition model demonstrating superior warning performance compared to any single parameter. Early postoperative vital sign monitoring and recognition of age-related atypical symptoms should be enhanced to improve the early identification and management of PE.

items.title: Intertwin umbilical vein diameter-to-abdominal circumference discordance in type 1 selective fetal growth restriction twins: association with risk of perinatal death in the smaller twin
items.abstract: ObjectiveSelective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) is a common complication of monochorionic-diamniotic twin pregnancies, and there is no unified clinical standard for determining the optimal timing of intervention. This study aimed to explore the value of ultrasound parameters for identifying risk of perinatal death (PND) of the smaller twin complicated with type 1 sFGR.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort study included 49 women with type 1 sFGR twin pregnancies who received regular prenatal ultrasound examination and had complete clinical and follow-up data. Cases with type 2/3 sFGR, fetal structural or chromosomal abnormalities, severe maternal complications, intrauterine intervention, or loss to follow-up were excluded. The primary outcome was PND of the smaller twin with type 1 sFGR, defined as either intrauterine death or 28-day neonatal death. The patients were divided into the PND group (n = 19) and the non-PND group (n = 30). Baseline ultrasonic indices were compared, with nested logistic regression, reclassification analysis and 500-sample bootstrap internal validation performed to assess incremental value and model stability.ResultsGestational age (GA) at diagnosis and the intra-abdominal umbilical vein diameter to abdominal circumference ratio (UV/AC) of the smaller twin in the PND group were significantly lower than those in the non-PND group (P < 0.05), whereas intertwin UV/AC discordance was significantly higher (P0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified two factors independently associated with PND in type 1 sFGR smaller twin: earlier GA at diagnosis (P = 0.013) and elevated intertwin UV/AC discordance (P = 0.006). The optimal cut-off of intertwin UV/AC discordance was 0.273% (AUC = 0.814, sensitivity 89.5%, specificity 53.3%). Reclassification analyses confirmed the incremental prognostic value of intertwin UV/AC discordance beyond conventional Doppler and clinical variables. The cutoff for GA at diagnosis yielded an AUC < 0.5, indicating reversed predictive performance.ConclusionGA at diagnosis and intertwin UV/AC discordance are independently associated with PND in type 1 sFGR smaller twin. Earlier type 1 sFGR diagnosis and higher intertwin UV/AC discordance are correlated with an increased PND risk. Intertwin UV/AC discordance may serve as a promising ultrasonic marker for antenatal risk stratification in type 1 sFGR.

items.title: Redefining mechanical ventilation in thoracic anesthesia: flow–controlled ventilation from bench to bedside—a narrative review
items.abstract: One–lung ventilation (OLV) remains a cornerstone of thoracic anesthesia but continues to challenge perioperative respiratory management. Restriction of ventilation to a reduced functional lung volume promotes ventilation–perfusion mismatch, alveolar instability, and exposure of the dependent lung to increased mechanical stress. Although contemporary lung–protective ventilation strategies have evolved considerably, postoperative pulmonary complications remain common, highlighting the need for innovative approaches to respiratory support. Flow–controlled ventilation (FCV) introduces a distinct physiological concept by actively controlling both inspiration and expiration through constant gas flow. Unlike conventional ventilation modes, which rely on passive exhalation, FCV enables linear pressure changes throughout the respiratory cycle and combines active expiratory control with direct intratracheal pressure monitoring and compliance–guided ventilator titration. This approach aims to improve ventilation efficiency while reducing mechanisms implicated in ventilator–induced lung injury. In this narrative review, we examine the physiological principles underlying FCV, discuss the technological innovations enabling its clinical application, and summarize current evidence from bench, preclinical, and clinical investigations. Experimental studies demonstrate improvements in respiratory mechanics, lung aeration, oxygenation, and mechanical power compared with conventional ventilation. Limited clinical data during OLV suggest potential improvements in oxygenation and carbon dioxide elimination at lower minute ventilation requirements; however, these findings are derived from small studies primarily evaluating physiological endpoints. Despite encouraging physiological results, important evidence gaps remain. Current clinical studies are limited by small sample sizes and focus predominantly on surrogate physiological outcomes. It remains unknown whether the observed improvements will translate into reductions in postoperative pulmonary complications or other patient–centered outcomes. By shifting attention from inspiration alone to the entire respiratory cycle, FCV challenges conventional paradigms of perioperative ventilation. Future multicenter outcome–driven trials will determine whether active expiratory control represents a meaningful advance in thoracic anesthesia or primarily a physiological innovation with limited clinical impact.

items.title: Editorial: New concepts, advances, and future trends in clinical research on eye diseases
Regression of severe sclerotic chronic graft-versus-host disease after a second haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a case report
items.abstract: Sclerotic chronic graft-versus-host disease (Scl-cGVHD) is a disabling fibrotic manifestation of cGVHD and frequently exhibits poor responsiveness to conventional immunosuppressive therapy. Therapeutic options remained limited, particularly in pediatric patients. An 8-year-old boy with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia underwent matched sibling donor allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) in January 2021. Four months later, he developed progressive cutaneous cGVHD that evolved into severe Scl-cGVHD, with diffuse skin thickening, painful fissures, ulceration, and multiple joint contractures, loss of independent ambulation, and complete dependence in activities of daily living. Skin biopsy demonstrated extensive dermal fibrosis, collagen deposition, and increased α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression. Despite multiple lines of immunosuppressive and targeted therapy, including corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, mycophenolate mofetil, ruxolitinib, rituximab, and other agents, the disease progressed, with the modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS) reaching 35. Because of refractory disease and disabling disease, a second haploidentical HSCT from his father was performed in September 2022. Following transplantation, disease progression ceased and gradual clinical improvement occurred. At 12 months, the mRSS decreased from 35 to 2, with substantial recovery of skin flexibility and joint mobility. Repeat skin biopsy showed reduced collagen compactness and markedly decreased interstitial α-SMA expression, consistent with attenuation and remodeling of dermal fibrosis. Serial immune monitoring revealed progressive recovery of B- and NK-cell compartments and sustained T-cell reconstitution after the second transplantation, in contrast to prolonged B-cell depletion and limited NK-cell recovery after the first transplant. At 24 months, complete donor chimerism persisted, leukemia remained in remission, the mRSS reached 0, and the patient regained independent walking and activities of daily living. This case describes sustained clinical regression and histopathological attenuation of severe, established Scl-cGVHD following a second haploidentical HSCT. The temporal association with immune reconstitution raises the possibility that restoration of immune homeostasis may have contributed to disease remodeling. However, causality cannot be established from a single case. Given the substantial risks associated with second allo-HSCT, this approach should not be considered standard therapy and may be considered only in exceptional, highly selected patients after multidisciplinary risk-benefit assessment.

items.title: Clinical features and management of medication-induced persistent corneal epithelial defects due to topical ophthalmic medications
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate the impact of subacute preservative-containing eye drop usage on the ocular surface and to observe the clinical progression and management of medication-induced persistent corneal epithelial defects (MI-PCED).MethodsThis retrospective study evaluated 60 cases (60 eyes) diagnosed with MI-PCED from January 2020 to January 2024. Data on the type, frequency, and duration of topical medication usage were collected. A multidisciplinary pharmacovigilance assessment evaluated causality, severity, and preventability of the adverse events. Upon diagnosis, the offending medications were discontinued and replaced with low-toxicity, preservative-free alternatives. For advanced epithelial decompensation with stromal involvement (Grades III and IV), bandage contact lenses (BCL) and amniotic membrane transplantation (AMT) were integrated into an exploratory step-wise management approach to promote epithelial wound healing. Treatment efficacy was evaluated using slit-lamp examination and in vivo confocal microscopy (IVCM).ResultsThe clinical manifestation of MI-PCED initiated with epithelial roughness and dry eye symptoms, ultimately progressing to persistent epithelial defects and corneal ulcers. The severity of epithelial decompensation correlated significantly with the number of concurrent medications (P < 0.05), administration frequency (P < 0.001), and medication duration (P < 0.05). Pharmacovigilance evaluation classified 80.0% of cases as “Probable” adverse drug reactions, with 58.3% graded as moderate (Grade 2) and 41.7% as severe (Grade 3). Following 7–30 days of targeted regenerative therapy, the cure rates were 88.57% for Grade I, 90.91% for Grade II, 77.78% for Grade III, and 80.00% for Grade IV. The overall cure rate was 86.67%.ConclusionsThe severity of MI-PCED is heavily dependent on the type, subacute duration, and frequency of topical ophthalmic drug use. Management requires a flexible, step-wise strategy focused on restoring ocular surface homeostasis. This includes withdrawing toxic agents, preserving tear film stability with preservative-free tears, and strategically utilizing BCL and AMT to provide mechanical protection and biological support for severe epithelial decompensation.

items.title: Delayed diagnosis of selected thoracic and mediastinal conditions in young adults: a focused narrative review of clinical pitfalls, cognitive biases, and system barriers
items.abstract: BackgroundThoracic and mediastinal conditions affecting the esophagus, diaphragm, mediastinum, and airway carry considerable morbidity when diagnosis is delayed. Young adults are often perceived as low risk for serious thoracic disease, and low clinical suspicion, atypical symptoms, and cognitive and healthcare-system barriers can delay recognition.MethodsThis focused narrative review searched PubMed and Scopus, supplemented by Google Scholar, for studies published between January 2000 and May 2026, with selected earlier landmark studies retained where essential. Search terms included “thoracic surgical conditions,” “young adults,” “late diagnosis,” “misdiagnosis,” and “unusual presentation.” Five conditions were selected purposively to illustrate contrasting mechanisms and time-courses of diagnostic delay rather than to catalogue thoracic disease exhaustively. No formal systematic search protocol, study-level quality appraisal, or narrative-review quality instrument was applied.ResultsFive diagnostic categories are examined: esophageal perforation and Boerhaave syndrome, traumatic diaphragmatic injury, primary mediastinal germ cell tumors, airway tumors misdiagnosed as asthma, and Hodgkin lymphoma presenting as an anterior mediastinal mass. Hodgkin lymphoma is included as a mediastinal diagnostic pitfall because it resembles other anterior mediastinal tumors and requires histological sampling for definitive diagnosis. Together, these conditions illustrate how overlapping cognitive and systemic barriers contribute to diagnostic delay. The strength and age relevance of the supporting evidence differ markedly between conditions and are stated explicitly, as much of the foundational literature derives from broader adult populations rather than cohorts restricted to ages 18–40.ConclusionsDiagnostic delay reflects the combined effects of non-specific presentation, anchoring, premature closure, limited access to imaging, and delayed specialist referral. Consequences differ by condition: in acute mechanical and perforation emergencies, delays measured in hours may affect contamination, deterioration, and operative complexity, whereas in indolent mediastinal malignancies delay principally affects diagnostic complexity, symptom and psychological burden, and time to staging and treatment, while prognosis remains strongly influenced by histological subtype and tumor biology. Structured reassessment after an unexpected treatment response, timely cross-sectional imaging, disease-specific testing, and early specialist referral are practical measures available to first-contact clinicians.

items.title: Coordinate attention and deformable convolution-enhanced YOLO for bilateral maxillary sinus segmentation, a paranasal sinus structure, in CT images
items.abstract: Accurate delineation of the maxillary sinuses in CT images is a relevant step supporting preoperative planning and the evaluation of sinonasal disease within otolaryngology. Manual contouring of these paranasal sinus structures is difficult and error-prone, since the surrounding anatomy is complex, bony structures are thin, and inter-patient variability is large. This paper proposes an instance segmentation framework that extends the YOLO11n-Seg architecture through the integration of Coordinate Attention (CoordAtt) modules and Deformable Convolutional Networks v2 (DCNv2), to improve spatial feature representation and boundary precision for the right and left maxillary sinuses in CT images. CoordAtt encodes directional spatial context along horizontal and vertical axes to enhance anatomical localisation, while DCNv2 replaces selected fixed-kernel convolution layers with adaptive deformable sampling to better capture irregular and thin-walled sinus boundaries. The proposed model was trained and evaluated on the publicly available NasalSeg dataset, using all axial CT slices containing either maxillary sinus from 130 patients (3,620 slices; 104/13/13 patients across training/validation/test), and compared against three YOLO-family baselines (YOLOv8n-Seg, YOLO11n-Seg, and YOLO26n-Seg). On the 382-slice test set (13 patients), the proposed model achieved a mask mAP50 of 93.07% and mask mAP50-95 of 74.49%, outperforming the three baselines by up to +4.60 and +3.30 percentage points, respectively, and a box mAP50 of 91.00% and mAP50-95 of 75.83%. A component-wise ablation study confirmed that this improvement arises from the joint use of CoordAtt and DCNv2 rather than from either mechanism alone, and patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals and paired significance testing confirmed the statistical robustness of the observed gains. These results represent proof-of-concept evidence that coordinate-aware attention and deformable convolution can be effectively integrated into a YOLO-based instance segmentation pipeline for bilateral maxillary sinus delineation from CT.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a machine-learning model for 3-year mortality after lung cancer resection: an online risk calculator and nomogram
items.abstract: BackgroundLung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and postoperative risk stratification may support individualized surveillance after pulmonary resection. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an exploratory prediction model for 3-year postoperative mortality using routinely available clinical, pathological, and laboratory variables, while explicitly addressing outcome ascertainment, model calibration, and the limitations of a single-center retrospective cohort.MethodsLASSO regression was used for feature selection, followed by a comparison of seven algorithms: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, XGBoost, and LightGBM. Model discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve performance were evaluated in a 7:3 internal hold-out split. The final model was selected primarily according to an internal-validation AUC, with calibration and classification metrics considered jointly. A web-based calculator and a nomogram were developed from the final model.ResultsIn the final outcome-ascertained analytic sample, 166 of 350 patients (47.43%) were classified as having died within 36 months and 184 (52.57%) were alive beyond 36 months. This proportion describes the event composition of the selected analytic cohort and should not be interpreted as a population-level postoperative mortality estimate. Six predictors were retained by LASSO: T stage, airway dissemination, pleural invasion, Ki-67 index, BMI, and direct bilirubin. Random Forest showed perfect apparent discrimination in the training set (AUC = 1.00) but decreased to 0.73 in validation. Logistic regression achieved the highest validation AUC (0.79; 95% CI, 0.70–0.87), with an accuracy of 0.75, an F1 score of 0.73, and a Brier score of 0.187, and was therefore selected as the final model.ConclusionThe final logistic regression model provided moderate internal discrimination and an interpretable framework for exploratory 3-year mortality risk estimation after lung cancer resection. The nomogram and web-based calculator facilitated model visualization, but the outcome-ascertained analytic cohort, potential event enrichment, and absence of external validation limited the interpretation of absolute risk and direct clinical application. Therefore, an independent multicenter and prospective validation with appropriate recalibration is required.

items.title: Correction: Comparative effectiveness and dose–response relationship of exercise-based interventions for muscle mass in older women with sarcopenia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
When CKM Syndrome Stage Is Not a Severity Scale: Audiometric Hearing Thresholds in Older U.S. Adults
items.abstract: Objective: To examine whether bilateral four-frequency pure-tone average (PTA4) increased across operational cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stages and assess associations with individual CKM components. Design: Cross-sectional National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic analysis. Survey-weighted models adjusted for demographics, education, smoking, and noise exposure. Study sample: Adults aged 70-79 years (n = 994); stage analysis n = 285; waist model n = 778. Results: Covariate-adjusted mean bilateral PTA4 thresholds did not increase consistently across stages. No planned Stage 2-4 comparison met the Holm criterion; Stage 4 minus Stage 3 was 4.45 dB HL (95% CI, -0.61 to 9.51; Holm p = 0.246). Stage 2-4-only heterogeneity was not supported (p = 0.197). The five-stage omnibus was significant (p < 0.001), but inference was limited by sparse lower-stage support, including one Stage 0 participant. Waist circumference alone met the nine-test Holm criterion: +1.57 dB HL per 10 cm (95% CI, 0.74 to 2.39; Holm p = 0.00547). Conclusions: Greater waist circumference was associated with higher PTA4, but this cross-sectional association does not establish a hearing benefit from reducing waist circumference. These data do not establish operational CKM stage as a graded indicator of PTA4 in adults aged 70-79 years.
items.authors: Le, D. M.; Tran, S. T.; Nguyen, V. C.

items.title: Transducin: an open-source pipeline recovering SNOMED-CT coded measurements from the undocumented Optopol .OPT and Zeiss Cirrus private-tag formats as DICOM Structured Reports
items.abstract: Background. Quantitative optical coherence tomography (OCT) measurements are essential for retinal disease monitoring, yet leading vendors store acquisition data in undocumented proprietary formats or encode measurements exclusively in private DICOM tags inaccessible to open systems. Methods. We present Transducin, an open-source Python library that reverse- engineers, through systematic binary analysis cross referenced against DICOM exported metadata from the same studies, the undocumented Optopol REVO FC130 and REVO 60 .OPT binary format and extracts quantitative measurements from Zeiss Cirrus HD-OCT 500 private DICOM tags, generating TID 1500 Structured Reports with SNOMED-CT coded findings for both platforms. A novel finding is that a scan-geometry parameter recorded by the OCT device (OCTPARAMS tag 23, the horizontal position of the foveal or disc reflex relative to scan center) encodes ocular laterality through its arithmetic sign (an anatomical consequence of the fovea's nasal position relative to the optic disc) enabling automated laterality inference that requires no operator data entry or filename convention. Results. The validation corpus comprised 475 Optopol .OPT files across two clinical sites: 387 at Site A (73 patients) and 88 at Site B (Queretaro); spanning three device models and four SOCT software versions, with 100% parse success across nine acquisition types. Cross-version compatibility was confirmed across SOCT versions 11.5.0-21.5.0, spanning approximately eight years of software development. The Zeiss Cirrus pipeline generated TID 1500 SRs for all 41 applicable studies (100%), yielding CMT 203-630 m and RNFL 53-123 m across a clinically representative range. The laterality-inference hypothesis was validated across 18 files from two device models and two software versions with 100% accuracy. Conclusions. Transducin provides the first publicly documented specification of the Optopol .OPT format and the first open-source multivendor pipeline generating SNOMED-CT coded DICOM Structured Reports from both Optopol REVO and Zeiss Cirrus devices, closing a gap explicitly confirmed by both manufacturers' own documentation. The code is available at https://github.com/oftalmos-org/transducin (Apache License 2.0).
items.authors: Jaurrieta Hinojos, J. N.; Palomares Ordonez, J. L.; Chacon Hinojos, J. F.; Folgueras Batres, M. A.

items.title: Exposure Records Preserved by Two Users of Japan's COVID-19 Contact-Confirming Application During the Seventh Wave: A Descriptive Study
items.abstract: Introduction: Japan's COVID-19 Contact-Confirming Application (COCOA) stopped functioning in November 2022, and the records held on users' devices were lost with it. We describe the exposure records preserved by two users during the seventh wave of COVID-19 in Japan and the changes around the revision of full mandatory case reporting on September 26, 2022. Methods: We analyzed exposure windows (date, duration, and minimum attenuation) contained in files exported from the app. Observer 1 worked at a hospital in Tokyo and commuted almost exclusively by private car; Observer 2 lived in Kyoto Prefecture and spent most of the time at home. Seven-day rolling sums of exposure windows were compared descriptively with daily new case counts in each prefecture. Results: During the common pre-revision period (April 3 to September 25, 2022; 176 days), Observer 1 recorded 358 exposure windows and Observer 2 recorded 261. The rolling sums rose in July and fell in September, as did new case counts (r-squared = 0.807 and 0.397), but week-on-week changes corresponded weakly (r-squared = 0.183 and 0.002). Of the windows in this period, 97.2% and 93.1% had a minimum attenuation of 65 dB or more, the bucket given the lowest weight in the notification decision. After the revision, Observer 1 recorded three windows in 27 days (45 in the preceding 27 days), and Observer 2 recorded none in 23 days (25 in the preceding 27 days). Conclusions: The exposure-window records of two users rose and fell with the seventh wave, although the correspondence of week-to-week changes was limited. Recorded windows decreased after the revision, but the effects of the policy change, the supply of diagnosis keys, app usage, and operating-system updates cannot be separated. This descriptive report does not evaluate the preventive effectiveness of COCOA. It shows that indicator definitions, retrieval dates, and the history of software and policy changes are essential when records left on users' devices are analyzed after the fact.
items.authors: Nakagawa, S.; Kumagai, S.; Yamamoto, A.

items.title: DualStream-MTCA: A Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Joint Prediction and Early Detection of Sepsis and Heart Failure in Adult Intensive Care
items.abstract: Objective: Sepsis and heart failure produce overlapping early physiological signs in intensive care but call for opposite treatments, yet existing models predict one condition at a time. We built one model for both. Methods: DualStream-MTCA combines two bidirectional long short-term memory encoders, for 48 hours of hourly vital signs and 7 days of daily laboratory results, with multi-head cross-attention, gradient-boosted-tree leaf embeddings and two task heads trained under uncertainty weighting. A refined configuration adds per-window aggregates, static patient features, self-supervised encoder pretraining and a five-seed ensemble with Monte Carlo dropout. Development used 53,229 adult stays from MIMIC-IV version 3.1; the frozen models were applied to 102,695 stays from the eICU Collaborative Research Database. Results: At a prediction time 48 hours after admission, the refined ensemble reached an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.867 for sepsis and 0.899 for heart failure internally, against 0.832 and 0.857 for the baseline model. Isotonic regression brought expected calibration error below 0.015. For positives whose onset followed the prediction time by 4 to 12 hours, the area dropped to 0.66 to 0.70. Externally, the refined ensemble scored 0.750 for sepsis and 0.786 for heart failure, against 0.711 and 0.821 for the baseline model. Conclusion: A single multi-task model matched its single-task variants on both conditions, but discrimination fell under strictly anticipatory prediction and across sites, where static features carried little usable signal. Significance: To our knowledge, this is the first model built specifically to predict both conditions jointly, with calibration, decision-curve and external evaluation.
items.authors: Khdir, S. A.; Ahmed, O. H.

items.title: Not in Education Employment or Training (NEET) Trajectories Across Adolescence and Early Adulthood and Subsequent Mental Health
items.abstract: In 3,792 participants from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children, we examined whether repeatedly being Not in Education, Employment or Training (NEET) between ages 16 and 33 was associated with mental health at age 33. Each additional NEET occasion was associated with higher odds of depression (OR: 1.29, 95%CI: 1.18-1.40), anxiety (1.21, 1.11-1.32), lower life satisfaction (1.53, 1.40-1.68) and a recent suicide attempt (1.51, 1.28-1.77). Associations were dose-dependent for depression, life satisfaction and a recent suicide attempt, and strongest for first NEET at ages 25-33. Preventing repeated NEET and addressing mental health need at first NEET entry are potential intervention targets.
items.authors: Kwong, A. S. F.; Elsden, E.

items.title: Methylation-driven Cancer Genes and Methylation Profiling in Glioma: A Comparative Study between East Asian and non-Hispanic White Populations
items.abstract: Global incidence and outcomes of glioma have been found to vary significantly by region, however research into the disease continues to lack diversity. Here we investigated epigenetic patterns in glioma subtypes from cohorts collected from China and the USA. We retrospectively analysed the Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) datasets following reclassification of glioma subtypes based on the WHO 2021 central nervous system (CNS) tumour classification. We used DNA methylation and transcriptomics data to identify methylation-driven cancer genes in the CGGA cohort, assessed their prognostic value and compared against the non-Hispanic White cohort in the TCGA database to consider ethnic influence. Furthermore, we used machine learning classification and clustering techniques to identify methylation patterns in glioma subgroups. Here, we showed that DNA methylation profiles of CGGA glioblastomas have a methylation signature more similar to TCGA high-grade astrocytomas: 36.7% of CGGA glioblastomas (n=49) were identified as high-grade astrocytomas using classification modelling. Assessment of survival revealed that CGGA glioblastoma patients had a significantly better survival rate than non-Hispanic White glioblastoma patients (p = 0.037). Four key methylation-driven genes were identified in the CGGA glioblastoma samples: GLDN, PRKDC, S100A1 and NCAPH. Hypermethylation of GLDN significantly suppressed gene expression in all glioma subtypes in only the East Asian cohort; a gene that has not been previously described as a driver in gliomas. Together these data suggest alternative epigenetic mechanisms occurring in glioma subtypes of different ethnic populations, which is important for our understanding of glioma and strategies for personalized treatment.
items.authors: Newman, L.; Dunne, N.; Cheng, V. W.; Sharma-Oates, A.

items.title: Distinct Type 2 Diabetes Components Exert Contrasting Effects on Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Development
items.abstract: BackgroundType 2 diabetes (T2D) has been associated with reduced abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) risk and slower growth in observational studies, but the mechanism for this paradoxical association remains unclear. We hypothesized that T2Ds mechanistic heterogeneity obscures opposing, pathway-specific effects on AAA. MethodsWe performed two-sample Mendelian Randomization (MR) to investigate the effect of T2D (T2DGGI, 242,283 individuals with T2D and 1,569,730 without) on AAA (AAAgen, 37,214 individuals with AAA and 997,456 without) using 449 genetic instruments. We also performed MR within previously defined clusters representing different mechanisms of T2D. We extended the analysis to individual hyperglycemic, insulin-resistance, and insulin-sensitivity traits. Our hypothesis was tested in a porcine pancreatic elastase murine model of abdominal aortic aneurysm formation. ResultsOverall T2D liability showed no net association with AAA liability (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.96-1.04, P = 0.90), albeit with marked instrument heterogeneity (Cochrans Q = 1356, P = 5 x 10-92) and inconsistency across sensitivity analyses, with a notably protective MR-Egger result (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.80-0.94, P = 0.0011) and non-zero intercept (P = 2 x 10-4). MR of T2D on AAA within mechanistic clusters showed opposing effects: lipodystrophy (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.26-1.72) and obesity (OR 1.27, 95% CI 1.18-1.36) cluster membership associated with increased AAA risk, while beta-cell negative proinsulin (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.76-0.90) and beta-cell positive proinsulin (OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.80-0.93) clusters were protective. This pattern was robust to clustering method. Traits indexing hyperglycemia (fasting glucose, 2-hour glucose, hemoglobin A1c) were associated with reduced AAA risk, while traits indexing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, BMI, waist-hip ratio, triglyceride-to-HDL ratio) were associated with increased AAA risk. In mice, those treated with a high fructose diet as a model for insulin resistance showed increased growth of the abdominal aorta compared with controls, whereas those treated with pancreatoxin streptozotocin as a model for isolated hyperglycemia showed blunted growth. ConclusionDistinct components of T2D physiology may have differential effects on AAA development. Whereas insulin resistance may promote AAA, hyperglycemia appears to protect against it. Our findings support insulin sensitization as a rational direction for AAA pharmacotherapy and suggest that the pathways mediating the protective effect of hyperglycemia may harbor additional therapeutic targets.
items.authors: DeVaro, D.; Raghavan, S.; Walker, V.; Gaunt, T.; Larsson, S.; Levin, M. G.; Rhee, Y. H.; Tsao, P. S.; Yuan, S.; Damrauer, S. M.

items.title: Centenarians maintain cognition by resisting amyloid-β or decoupling it from tau propagation
items.abstract: Centenarians who maintain cognitive health provide a unique opportunity to investigate naturally occurring mechanisms that protect against Alzheimers disease. We examined the relationship between subregional amyloid-beta and p-tau distributions in the medial temporal lobe and cognitive performance in 112 centenarians. We show that amyloid-beta pathology was associated with increased parahippocampal, but not hippocampal, p-tau burden and lower cognitive performance. However, the majority of the centenarians maintained high cognitive performance until death, and they appeared to be protected against cognitive decline through two distinct mechanisms: 44% were resistant to amyloid-beta accumulation, while 28% harbored substantial amyloid-beta pathology but resisted downstream p-tau propagation. These findings suggest the existence of natural resilience mechanisms that uncouple amyloid-beta pathology from driving downstream pathogenic tau progression. Both mechanisms warrant further exploration, as they may offer complementary therapeutic entry-points: preventing the accumulation of A{beta} pathology altogether, or limiting downstream p-tau propagation once A{beta} pathology has already emerged.
items.authors: Rohde, S. K.; Luimes, M. C.; Rozemuller, A. J. M.; Hulsman, M.; van der Lee, S. J.; Sikkes, S. A. M.; Richardson, T. E.; Hoozemans, J. J. M.; Walker, J. M.; Holstege, H.

items.title: Persistently uneven deep brain stimulation management in Japan: a nationwide claims analysis, 2014-2024
items.abstract: BackgroundThe long-term benefit of deep brain stimulation (DBS) for neurological disorders depends on sustained post-implantation management, yet its geographic distribution remains poorly characterised. We aimed to describe regional variation, persistence, and longitudinal change in DBS management activity across Japan. MethodsWe used claims from the National Database of Health Insurance Claims (NDB) Open Data during 2014-2024. Annual billings for DBS management were expressed per million population. Annual between-prefecture unevenness was summarised by the Gini coefficient of the prefecture DBS management billing rate. We evaluated longitudinal trajectories and trends in DBS management billing rates relative to the national rate, and related baseline billing rates to subsequent trends. FindingsFrom 2014 to 2024, national DBS management billings increased from 18,659 to 27,233, totalling 258,408. Between-prefecture unevenness remained high throughout (Gini coefficient, 0.54 to 0.40), and its narrowing decelerated over the study period. In 2024, the prefecture at the 90th percentile still billed at 9.1 times the rate of the prefecture at the 10th. Of the 23 low-baseline prefectures, nine showed a subsequent decline in relative billing rate; nonetheless, lower baseline DBS management billing rates were associated with a more positive relative rate of change overall. InterpretationOngoing post-implantation DBS management activity was markedly uneven and persistent across Japan. The observations suggest that universal health coverage and national-level growth do not by themselves ensure equitable long-term DBS treatment. This nationwide, longitudinal description could inform policies aimed at reducing geographic barriers to long-term specialist care across healthcare systems FundingNone.
items.authors: Tanimura, J.; Hashimoto, T.

items.title: Smartphone Passive Digital Phenotyping in Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration
items.abstract: IntroductionFrontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) is a devastating disease that commonly results in early onset dementia, yet its rarity and heterogeneity limit large-scale research and clinical trials. Remote monitoring via low-burden digital health tools may overcome these barriers. We evaluated clinical utility of passive smartphone monitoring in FTLD using a multi-domain mobile assessment platform. MethodsParticipants were 567 adults (53% clinically normal, 21% prodromal FTLD, 26% symptomatic FTLD) who completed an in-person study visit and downloaded the ALLFTD Mobile App on their personal smartphones. The app delivered unsupervised cognitive tests and passively collected continuous data on battery percentage (proxy for smartphone use) and step count. Longitudinal follow-up included smartphone monitoring and annual in-person study visits. Primary analyses examined associations between passive smartphone features and markers of disease severity at baseline and longitudinally, and tested whether passive features added incremental value beyond app-based cognitive testing. ResultsPassive smartphone features were feasible to collect and showed excellent reliability with 0.9). Features capturing smartphone use and movement demonstrated sensitivity to gold-standard clinical measures of disease severity both at baseline and longitudinally. A classification model combining passive features, the app-based cognitive composite score, and demographics detected longitudinal functional decline (AUC=0.89); passive features alone (AUC=0.84) performed comparably to a cognitive screener (AUC=0.85). DiscussionPassive smartphone monitoring is a valid, zero-burden measure of disease severity and progression in FTLD that adds modest incremental value beyond app-based cognitive testing. Findings support its use as a scalable digital endpoint in longitudinal FTLD research.
