Even in this extreme steric regime, gearing remains accessible with barriers of ~15 kcal mol–1 and is only weakly affected by the iodine substituent, whereas enantiomerization requires substantially higher-energy rotational pathways. These findings provide a mechanistic picture of molecular motion under extreme steric constraints and establish overcrowded iodanemediated rearrangement as a route to previously inaccessible C–O atropisomeric architectures.
items.authors: Bin Li, Jun Kikuchi, Arimasa Matsumoto, Naohiko Yoshikai

items.title: GXNU MolStudio: An Integrated Open-Source Platform for Molecular Visualization and Quantum Chemical Analysis
items.abstract: We report GXNU MolStudio, an open-source, bilingual (Chinese/English) desktop application that integrates real-time molecular visualization with a broad suite of quantum chemical analyses in a single interactive environment. MolStudio embeds a purpose-built OpenGL 3.3 renderer that presents molecules, orbitals, and property-colored isosurfaces in a publication-ready style, and couples it to scripted invocations of the external wavefunction analysis program Multiwfn. The current version provides 14 panels (11 analysis panels plus 3 workflow panels) covering: orbital browsing and isosurface generation (including spin-density visualization for open-shell systems); six atomic charge schemes (ADCH, Hirshfeld, Mulliken, CM5, SCPA, and VDD); Mayer bond orders; NBO donor–acceptor (E(2)) analysis; electrostatic potential (ESP) surfaces with extrema and surface-area distributions; IGMH/IRI weak-interaction analysis; QTAIM topology; ETS-NOCV energy decomposition; molecular planarity parameters (MPP); IRC energy/bond-order profiles; distortion–interaction (DI) decomposition; the energetic span model (ESM); and activation strain scans along the IRC (ASM), multi-CUB overlay, and IRC splitting. All panels share one canvas and one atomic-picking protocol, so that results from different analyses can be compared immediately on the same structure. A retained VMD/Tachyon channel delivers ray-traced journal-quality figures in more than 30 curated styles. MolStudio is distributed as Python source (PyQt5, Python ≥ 3.8) and as a standalone Windows executable, under the GNU General Public License, version 3 (GPLv3only). Its rendering pipeline is a Python port of the GPLv3-licensed IboView engine — a derivative relationship that is declared explicitly in Section 7 and itemized in the code repository — and all third-party components are credited. The software is freely available at https://cnb.cool/chem311/GXNU-MolStudio.
items.authors: Cheng Hou

items.title: Solid-Phase Standard Enthalpies of Formation from SMILES with a Calibrated Per-Molecule Uncertainty: Application to a 13 606-Compound CHONFCl Inventory
items.abstract: The standard enthalpy of formation of a solid, ∆fH ◦(s, 298 K), governs the detonation performance and the thermal hazard of an energetic material, yet it is measured for only a few hundred compounds, and 30 % of the compounds measured more than once carry determinations that disagree by more than 20 kJ mol−1. I report a route from a SMILES string to ∆fH ◦(s, 298 K) that returns, together with the value, a molecule-specific standard deviation calibrated against experiment. The gas-phase enthalpy is obtained from the ANI-2x neural network potential evaluated on a connectivity-based hierarchy (CBH-2, with CBH-1 fallback) isodesmic balance in which the nitro group is treated as a single pseudo-atom, without which the balance cannot be closed on a charge-separated nitrogen; a rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator correction supplies the thermal terms. The sublimation enthalpy is a 32-descriptor additive model fitted to 229 measurements harvested from the NIST Chemistry WebBook. Two systematic shifts that survive leave-one-out validation are removed. The uncertainty is a heteroscedastic Gaussian variance model. The whole chain is validated by a nested leave-one-out procedure in which the sublimation model, the acceptance threshold, the systematic shifts and the variance model are all re-estimated without the compound they predict, and that compound’s own gas-phase reference is withheld: over 281 compounds the mean absolute error is 26.1 kJ mol−1, the mean |z| is 0.80 against 0.80 expected for a well-calibrated Gaussian, and the coverage is 71.2 % at one standard deviation and 93.6 % at two, against 68.3 % and 95.4 % expected. For scale, independent experimental determinations of the same solid deviate from their own median by 7.6 kJ mol−1 on average, so two determinations of one compound typically differ by about twice that. The procedure was applied to an inventory of 13 606 CHONFCl compounds; 13 267 (97.5 %) were predicted in 314 core-hours on a single desktop machine, the remainder being open-shell radicals outside the domain of ANI-2x. I state explicitly, and quantify, the size beyond which the uncertainty model itself extrapolates.
items.authors: Luc E. Brunet

items.title: Data-driven models for performance prediction in a microalgae-based wastewater treatment process
items.abstract: Microalgae-based wastewater treatment has the potential to advance tertiary phosphorus recovery while producing biomass for resource valorization. The development of reliable near-term prediction models can help reduce system upsets, support proactive process control, and optimize resource utilization. In this study, Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LGBM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models were comparatively evaluated for predicting effluent ammonium, nitrate, and orthophosphate concentrations and biomass dynamics in a full-scale (568 m 3 ·d -1 ) microalgal system using 25 months of operational and microalgal community structure data. LSTM consistently achieved the highest prediction accuracy while effectively capturing system upset events. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis provided interpretable insights into feature importance across both feature and temporal dimensions, with SHAP-guided feature reduction substantially reducing computational requirements without compromising predictive performance. Benchmarking against the mechanistic process model further identified the complementary application niches of mechanistic and data-driven approaches, providing practical guidance for model selection.
items.authors: Ga-Yeong Kim, JooMan Kim, Jeremy S. Guest

items.title: High-Field Spin Dynamics of Photoexcited Pentacene at 9.2 T by Time-Resolved Pulsed EPR and Vector DC Magnetic-Field Sensing
items.abstract: Photoexcited triplet spin states of pentacene molecules are promising for dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) and quantum sensing, yet their spin properties at high magnetic fields remain largely unexplored. Here, we study the high field spin dynamics of the photoexcited pentacene using highfrequency time-resolved pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) at 260 GHz (∼ 9.2 T). Using pulsed EPR synchronized with optical excitation, we determine triplet sublevel populations, decay rates, spin relaxations, and the g-tensor. The transient triplet remains a strongly non-Boltzmann sublevel population, with a dominant |TX⟩ population of 0.86 ± 0.05, while the triplet lifetimes, spin-lattice relaxation, and coherence remain favorable for triplet-DNP and quantum sensing applications. We further develop a vector DC magnetic-field sensing protocol that combines the transition resonances of the two crystallographically inequivalent pentacene sites with orientation-dependent triplet decay to determine the field magnitude and orientation. These results establish the high-field spin properties of photoexcited pentacene and provide a foundation for its triplet-DNP and quantum sensing at high magnetic fields.
items.authors: Duhan Zhang, Zeyu Wang, Johan van Tol, Yifan Quan

items.title: AI-Driven Optimization of Electrochemical Fertilizer Processes
items.abstract: Conventional fertilizer production relies on centralized, fossil-fuel-intensive processes such as Haber–Bosch ammonia synthesis, with high energy demand and associated carbon emissions. Electrochemical routes to nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizers offer a potentially decentralized, renewable-powered alternative, but their practical performance remains limited by the interaction of catalyst structure, electrolyte composition, reactor architecture, and operating conditions. These variables do not act independently: fertilizer synthesis is fundamentally a coupled, high-dimensional optimization problem that is difficult to address by varying one factor at a time. This chapter argues that artificial intelligence becomes genuinely useful for this problem not as an isolated computational tool, but as a layer connecting experimental and sensor data with prediction, optimization, and control. The chapter examines four electrochemical fertilizer pathways nitrogen reduction, nitrate reduction, urea synthesis, and phosphorus recovery alongside the functional materials and electrode architectures used to catalyze them. It then considers the reactors, analytical instrumentation, and real-time, in-situ sensors that generate the data on which these AI applications depend, treating this measurement infrastructure as inseparable from AI-enabled optimization. Three distinct roles for AI and machine learning are developed: discovering and screening catalyst candidates across combinatorial design spaces; predicting process behavior under coupled and time-varying operating conditions; and identifying and maintaining optimal conditions through Bayesian optimization, multi-objective search, and autonomous control. Techno-economic and life-cycle assessment are introduced as additional decision criteria, since chemical performance alone cannot define an optimal process once cost and environmental impact are considered. A fully integrated, autonomous electrochemical fertilizer platform has not yet been demonstrated in the literature reviewed here. Instead, the chapter shows that individual components of such a system, together with several partial integrations from adjacent process industries, already exist and provide a technically credible foundation for future integration. Data scarcity, the DFT–experiment gap, sensor reliability, reproducibility, interpretability, and scale-up nevertheless remain major barriers to realizing this integration in practice.
items.authors: Muhammad Bilal

items.title: Mechanochemical Degradation of Activated Carbon-Adsorbed PFAS and Fluorinated Gases
items.abstract: Fluorochemicals are widely used in modern society due to their unique and valuable properties. From the perspective of sustainable fluorine resource utilization, technologies that enable the recovery and reuse of fluorine from waste or captured fluorochemicals are crucial. However, efficient strategies for recovering fluorine from these materials remain limited. Herein, we report a mechanochemical strategy for the direct conversion of activated carbon-adsorbed PFAS and fluorinated gases into potassium fluoride (KF), a valuable fluorination reagent, by ball milling with potassium metal. The process proceeds rapidly and efficiently under solvent-free conditions. The method is applicable to a variety of PFAS, including perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluoroheptanoic acid (PFHpA), and perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS), as well as fluorinated gases such as SF6, HFC-125, and HFC-23. This work provides a sustainable strategy toward a fluoro-circular economy through the recovery of fluorine as a valuable chemical resource.
items.authors: Masashi Hattori, Kouki Nagano, Moe Fujishiro, Kanako Inoo, Yosuke Kishikawa, Zhengyu Zhao

items.title: Lighting the Way to Sustainability with Refractory Plasmonic Materials
items.abstract: The search for plasmonic materials that combine strong light-matter interactions with stability under demanding operating conditions has driven growing interest in transition metal nitrides and carbides. These refractory materials offer tunable optical properties, thermal and chemical stability, and diverse electronic structures that distinguish them from conventional noble-metal plasmonic materials. This Review examines the development of refractory plasmonic materials from their fundamental photophysical properties and synthesis to their use in water-energy systems, climate-resilient infrastructure, and solar-driven chemical transformations. Attention is given to how composition, stoichiometry, particle morphology, and surface chemistry influence localized surface plasmon resonance, hot-carrier dynamics, and photothermal conversion. We critically assess the sustainability of refractory plasmonics beyond noble-metal replacement, considering resource availability and criticality, synthesis and processing requirements, material complexity, and functional lifetime. Finally, we outline key challenges and emerging opportunities in positioning refractory plasmonic materials as the cornerstone of a sustainable economy.
items.authors: Vanshika Jain, Dreenan Shea, Blaine G. Fiss, Mita Dasog

items.title: Continuous carbon capture and release using an aqueous oxygen-tolerant redox electrolyte in symmetric flow cells
items.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 capture provides a promising pathway for carbon management under ambient conditions, yet practical deployment remains limited by system complexity and energy losses associated with oxygen sensitivity, crossover, and overpotentials. Here we report a fluoflavine disulfonate (FFDS)-based symmetric flow reactor for continuous electrochemical CO2 capture. The symmetric configuration generates spatially separated alkaline catholyte and acidic anolyte through a proton-coupled electron transfer process, enabling simultaneous electrochemical regeneration of sorbent, CO2 absorption as (bi)carbonate, and CO2 release. The system demonstrates excellent stability and high oxygen tolerance under simulated flue gas conditions. Furthermore, the CO2 release rate can be regulated by varying the applied current density. Proton crossover is identified as a parasitic transport pathway that compromises energy efficiency. Its impact can be mitigated through buffer regulation and ultimately eliminated by using an industrial packed column to maximize gas–liquid contact. An isolated dual-loop cycling mode further enables simultaneous CO2 capture and release throughout charge–discharge cycling, improving electron utilization under pure-CO2 release conditions. A preliminary techno-economic analysis identifies electricity consumption as the dominant cost contributor, while the cost associated with the redox-active molecule is negligible. Overall, this work establishes a compact, modular, plug and play symmetric electrochemical platform for continuous CO2 enrichment under near-practical operating conditions.
items.authors: Xingqi Wang, Juwen Su, Kaiping Zhu, Xinglei Zhao, Liuchuan Tong, Yan Jing

items.title: Approaching Chemical Accuracy for Neutral and Ionic Water Clusters with the bn-r2SCAN Meta-GGA
items.abstract: Gas-phase neutral and ion–water clusters are fundamental models for hydrogen bonding, many-body interactions, proton transfer, and ionic hydration in liquid water and aqueous environments, and they are stringent tests for density functional approximations: semilocal functionals without exact exchange or an explicit self-interaction correction have typically described their interaction and binding energies poorly. The non-self-consistent SCAN@HF approach was recently shown to describe water clusters and liquid water with high accuracy, but subsequent analysis demonstrated that this performance arises largely from cancellation between a substantial functional-driven error and an opposing error introduced by the overlocalized Hartree–Fock density. Here we assess a new self-consistent meta-generalized gradient approximation, bonded-norm r2SCAN (bn-r2SCAN), for neutral, protonated, and deprotonated water clusters and for alkali-and halide–water complexes. bn-r2SCAN approaches chemical accuracy across these diverse systems, with overall mean unsigned binding-energy errors of 0.33− 1.04 kcal/mol for the benchmark sets considered, and substantially improves upon r2SCAN. Error decomposition shows that this accuracy does not rest on the near-total cancellation of large opposing errors underlying SCAN@HF: for the BEGDB dataset, the mean functional-and density-driven errors of bn-r2SCAN are 0.34 and −0.89 kcal/mol, and even for the largest clusters both remain a small fraction of the total binding energy, whereas for SCAN@HF the functional-driven error of SCAN and the nonvariational density over-localization introduced by the Hartree–Fock density each exceed 5 kcal/mol and cancel to within a few tenths. Notably, bn-r2SCAN was parametrized using band gaps and lattice constants (not weak bonds) of simple solids, making its performance for aqueous clusters a demanding test of transferability and identifying it as a self-consistent and computationally efficient route to modeling water and aqueous systems.
items.authors: Chandra Shahi, Adrienn Ruzsinszky, John P. Perdew

items.title: Solid-state synthesis of high-purity mixed-chalcogenide perovskites
items.abstract: Recently, chalcogenide perovskites that are fully inorganic and composed of earth-abundant elements are emerging as non-toxic alternatives to established lead-halide perovskite materials. However, chalcogenide perovskite compositions relevant for optoelectronic applications such as solar cells remain largely unexplored due to the complex, high-temperature synthesis routes involved and difficulties in obtaining high purities. Here, we present a new solid-state synthesis route for facile fabrication of mixed-chalcogenide perovskite powders BaZr(S 1−x Se x ) 3 , where 0 ≤ x ≤ 0.3. We obtain high-purity chalcogenide perovskite powders at moderate temperatures (600 ◦ C) and short reaction times (24 hours). We demonstrate that precursor selection and chalcogen stoichiometry can effectively be used to control the perovskite composition. By increasing Se content (x), the band gaps of the mixed-chalcogenide perovskites can be controllably tuned from 1.83 to 1.58 eV, spanning the desired range for single-and multi-junction solar cells. Broadly, our findings establish a generalisable synthesis method for preparing several mixed-chalcogenide perovskite compositions, including BaZr(S 1−x Se x ) 3 and BaHf(S 1−x Se x ) 3 .
items.authors: Mo El Maoued, Benjamin M. Gallant, Matteo Paloni, Luis Simbari, Shams Elnawawi, Matteo Salvalaglio

items.title: Programmable aggregation of photosensitizer in multi- organelles for cancer therapy
items.abstract: The precise spatiotemporal control of subcellular drug distribution remains a central therapeutic challenge. Here, a stimulus-responsive aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photosensitizer (TBPBB) is utilized to achieve controllable aggregation switching between two distinct organelles that enables sequential dual-organelle destruction. Actively delivered to tumors by hypoxia-tropic Bacillus subtilis, TBPBB first aggregates at mitochondria, generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) under light exposure, triggering bond cleavage to form a second AIE species (TBP) that re-aggregates at lipid droplets and generates ROS more efficiently. The sequential targeting and destruction of dual organelles, together with ROS-triggered bacterial lysis, induce ferroptosis, apoptosis and antitumor immunity, collectively amplifying therapeutic efficacy. In a breast cancer model, this system achieves a 92.4% tumour growth inhibition with negligible organ toxicity. This paradigm establishes a generalizable strategy for programmable aggregation of therapeutic agents and multi-organelle destruction, readily adaptable to other organelle pairs by substituting the stimuli-responsive moieties or targeting fragments.
items.authors: Lin Kong, Yun-hao Chen, Shun-yi Wang, Wei He, Meng-li Liu, Zheng Zhao

items.title: EVALUATING MOLECULAR DYNAMICS FRAMES FOR BINDING AFFINITY PREDICTION AND VIRTUAL SCREENING
items.abstract: Motivation: Machine-learning scoring functions are typically trained on static crystallographic structures, although protein-ligand recognition is inherently dynamic. It remains unclear whether MD derived conformations provide transferable information or instead shift the training data away from experimentally observed binding geometries. Results: We generated 20 ns molecular dynamics trajectories for 2,502 protein–ligand complexes and evaluated five scoring function architectures trained on crystallographic structures and MD-derived frames using four different sampling protocols. Across the CASF-2016 and CASF-2013 affinity benchmarks, MD-only training generally reduced predictive performance, whereas augmenting crystallographic structures with MD data improved four of the five architectures. Averaged across models, benchmarks, and sampling protocols, augmentation increased PCC by 0.072 and reduced RMSE by 0.165 relative to MD-only training. A nearest-neighbor analysis showed that the benefits of augmen-tation were not restricted to complexes similar to frames, arguing against a simple similarity-based explanation. The results suggest improvements were connected with exposing models to controlled structural perturbations around experimentally observed binding poses. Overall, MD conformations were most effective as augmentation rather than replacement for crystallographic training data. Availability: MD frames used for model training are available at: (https://zenodo.org/ records/20443988).
items.authors: Jakub Poziemski, Pawel Siedlecki

items.title: Alkynyl Flexion as a Design Principle for Cryoelastic Phosphorescent Crystals
items.abstract: Achieving cryogenic mechanical flexibility and persistent phosphorescence simultaneously is challenging because cooling suppresses molecular motion, favoring long-lived emission while limiting the structural adaptability required for elastic deformation. Alkynyl-engineering enables the C≡C unit to function beyond its conventional role as a conjugated linker, with directional C≡C···π-hole interactions serving as a key determinant of crystal packing and mechanical response. Three positional isomers, p-TPA-TRZ, m-TPA-TRZ, and o-TPA-TRZ, were designed to examine how molecular geometry controls this interaction topology while retaining the same TPA donor, TRZ acceptor, and alkynyl linker. These isomers yield six distinct single crystal forms, each exhibiting unique packing structures, emission properties, and mechanical responses. Flexible crystals consistently display C≡C···π-hole contacts that extend into alkynyl-directed interaction networks, whereas the non-flexible crystals lack this topology. The results demonstrate that specific intermolecular interactions can generate emergent crystal-level mechanical behavior through their geometric organization and propagation across the lattice. Remarkably, the flexible crystals retain their mechanical adaptability at 77 K, with persistent phosphorescence. These results establish a molecular-tocrystal design principle in which alkynyl-directed C≡C···π-hole interactions organize crystal packing to generate emergent cryogenic elasticity and persistent phosphorescence.
items.authors: Jiaqi Peng, Zheng Zhao, Zijie Qiu, Parvej Alam, Ben Zhong Tang

items.title: Electronic Control of Composition in Multicomponent oDCPD Fragment Functionalization
items.abstract: Deconstruction of poly(dicyclopentadiene)-co-cleavable comonomer (pDCPD-co-CC) thermosets generates oligomers with C=C bonds amenable to chemical functionalization; strategies for doing so remain limited. We report a one-step electrophilic multicomponent post-polymerization modification of deconstruction-relevant model hydroxyl-terminated poly(dicyclopentadiene) oligomers (oDCPD-OH), installing bromine, ether, and sulfonamide motifs. Sulfonamide substituent electronics influence apparent alkene conversion and sulfonamide functional group installation in the isolated oligomers, with electron-poor aryl sulfonamides yielding higher functionalization than electron-rich aryl sulfonamides (32 mol%, and 1 mol%, respectively). Mixed p-CF3/p-NO2 sulfonamide feeds (9:1–1:3) were examined, systematically varying oligomer composition. The incorporated fraction of p-NO2 ranges from 18 to 86%, consistently exceeding its feed fraction and indicating preferential incorporation under competitive conditions. Functionalized fragments show composition-dependent thermal decomposition, with thermal decomposition temperature (Td,5%) ranging from 126 to 176 °C. These results establish electronically guided multicomponent post-polymerization functionalization as a strategy for systematically modulating oDCPD fragment composition.
items.authors: Janna Jeschke, Mariel J. Price, Jeremiah A. Johnson, Hatice Mutlu

items.title: Acylals Derived from Acrylic Anhydride as Latent Anhydride Crosslinkers for Catalyst-Free Vitrimers
items.abstract: Carboxylic anhydrides are attractive dynamic covalent bonds that undergo rapid bond exchange without external catalysts. In this study, acylals prepared from acrylic anhydrides and aromatic aldehydes were employed as latent carboxylic anhydride crosslinkers to introduce dynamic anhydride linkages into polymer networks via postpolymerization heat treatment. Model experiments using small molecules suggested that acylals themselves undergo bond exchange, although the exchange is considerably slower and proceeds via a dissociative mechanism. In contrast, carboxylic anhydrides undergo rapid bond exchange via an associative mechanism. Polymers containing acylal crosslinks exhibited slow stress relaxation and required a high temperature (220 °C) for reprocessing. Heat treatment converted the acylal crosslinks into carboxylic anhydride crosslinks, resulting in substantially faster stress relaxation, improved reprocessability, and decrosslinking via hydrolysis. The heat-treated network exhibited catalyst-free stress relaxation with an Arrhenius temperature dependence, demonstrating the formation of a carboxylic anhydride-based vitrimer.
items.authors: Yasuhiro Kohsaka, Sumire Hayakawa

items.title: Machine Learned Interatomic Forces as Inference-Time Physical Guidance for All-Atom Diffusion Peptide Design
items.abstract: Diffusion-based biomolecular generative models can efficiently explore peptidereceptor sequence-structure space, but the learned generative distribution does not explicitly represent the underlying atomistic potential-energy landscape. As a result, generated complexes may contain locally unfavorable atomic arrangements even when they remain plausible under the learned structural prior. Here, we develop an inferencetime physical guidance framework that couples machine learned interatomic potential (MLIP)-derived forces to the all-atom reverse diffusion trajectory of RFDiffusion3 for receptor-conditioned peptide design. Rather than applying energy minimization after generation, atomistic physical information is introduced before the joint sequencestructure trajectory termination. MLIP-derived forces therefore provide atomic coordinate corrections that are propagated through subsequent denoising steps, allowing physical information to influence not only atomic geometry but subsequent residue selection. The framework requires neither retraining nor modification of the pretrained diffusion model and uses late-stage force guidance, adaptive step-size control, and geometry-preserving projection to retain the underlying generative prior. Across eight receptor systems for peptide designs, MLIP guidance reduced peptidereceptor steric clashes by 24.7% and intrapeptide clashes by 37.4%, while promoting more hydrogen-bond-compatible interface geometries. Guided structures shifted toward more favorable energetic regions in both the guiding MACE potential and an independent MM/GBSA evaluation, with 82.4% of retained structures exhibiting more favorable MM/GBSA energetic estimates. These improvements were achieved with a median peptide backbone deviation of only 0.051 Å. Importantly, 95.0% of generated peptide sequences were preserved, whereas 5.0% underwent residue substitutions, demonstrating that physical guidance can feed back into sequence-structure generation without globally overriding the learned RFDiffusion3 distribution. This distinguishes inference-time physical guidance from post-generation relaxation, which optimizes only the coordinates at fixed chemical identity. More broadly, the results establish a general strategy for coupling pretrained biomolecular generators with differentiable atomistic energy models, enabling physical information to participate directly in molecular generation rather than serving only as a post hoc filter or refinement step.
items.authors: Biao Zeng, Youyi Song, Jinfeng Liu

items.title: Direct generation of a prototypical n-pentyl peroxy radical reveals how mixedfate chemical regimes shape product distributions
items.abstract: Organic peroxy radicals (RO2) are key branch points in atmospheric oxidation with competing fates in the troposphere: reaction with NO, reaction with HO2, self-/cross-reaction with another RO2, and isomerization. RO2 often react in mixed-fate regimes, yielding product distributions with a complex dependence on reactivity conditions. In traditional environmental chamber experiments, not all RO2 fates are equally accessible, and chemical regimes favoring RO2 self-/cross-reactions and isomerizations are poorly characterized. Here, we access these conditions in an environmental chamber via 1-iodopentane photolysis, monitoring product distributions with NH4 + chemical ionization mass spectrometry. We tune the relative importance of these reaction pathways by varying the initial conditions, spanning bimolecular lifetimes from ~100-2000 s. Across conditions, the major observed C5 product, C5H10O3 (~40-60% yield), requires at least one RO2 isomerization to form, demonstrating the importance of downstream RO2 unimolecular reactions even if they are not the major fate of upstream RO2. Model mechanisms partially reproduce observed product distributions but cannot quantitatively capture variations with changing RO2 fate. Discrepancies suggest poorly-understood RO2 cross-reactions substantially influence product distributions. Conditions favoring RO2 isomerization unintuitively enhance both fragmentation and accretion via downstream functionalized alkoxy and peroxy radical chemistry. Results illuminate important gaps in existing atmospheric reaction mechanisms when predicting product distributions in mixed-fate chemical regimes.
items.authors: Cooper K. Crabtree, Sara E. Murphy, Victoria P. Barber

items.title: Boundary-driven phase transformation in layered 3R In2Se3 captured by long range machine learning molecular dynamics
items.abstract: Layered In2Se3 switches between closely related crystalline van der Waals states, but its atomistic thermal pathway in rhombohedral 3R geometries remains unresolved because middle-Se motion within each quintuple layer (QL), inter-QL glide, freesurface morphology, and weak interlayer binding evolve together. Here we develop a PBE+D3(BJ)-trained MACERSGA interatomic potential that adds a reciprocal-space gated-attention long-range correction to a short-range MACE backbone. Compared with MACE trained on the same data, MACERSGA reduces test-set energy and force RMSEs by 83.8% and 17.7%, respectively, while preserving the PBE+D3(BJ) exfoliation binding curves of α-and β-like structures. Large-cell molecular dynamics examines 1QL vacuum slabs, 3QL vacuum slabs, and periodic 3QL cells containing one full 3R repeat. Heating and cooling ramps at 5 and 1 K ps−1, supported by fixed-temperature holds, reveal a boundary hierarchy in the finite-rate structural-change window. The 1QL vacuum slab shows structural change first, followed by the 3QL vacuum and periodic 3QL cells. The 3QL vacuum slab also undergoes substantially larger inter-QL glide than the periodic cell. Cooling the α-heated structures directly tests whether the transformed states retain boundary-specific structural memory on the simulated timescale. Upon cooling, both 3QL systems retain transformed local environments near θ ≈ 57◦ at room temperature rather than returning to high-θ α, yet preserve distinct inter-QL registries and out-of-plane morphologies inherited directly from their boundary-specific heating pathways. These results show how nanoscale boundary conditions shape transformation pathways and retained interlayer registry in layered In2Se3, revealing structural memory relevant to nonvolatile crystalline memory and neuromorphic switching concepts.
items.authors: Igor Evangelista, Michaela Cohen, Atul C. Thakur, Anderson Janotti, Chris Benmore, Tingyi Gu

items.title: MACHINE LEARNING FOR CELLULOSE MEMBRANES: A REPRESENTATION–MODEL–TASK FRAMEWORK FOR SMALL-DATA REGIMES
items.abstract: Cellulose membranes are a small-data problem with a chemically ambiguous object. A polymorphic matrix, three chemically inequivalent hydroxyls at C2, C3 and C6, and a two-stage fabrication route make representation — not model architecture — the binding constraint on machine learning in this field, and this is why the toolkit that succeeded for gas-separation polymers and thin-film-composite membranes does not transfer to cellulose unchanged. This review organises the methodology around that claim. It first sets out why cellulose membranes remain of interest and where they fail, then shows that the existing computational treatment of cellulose is stratified into layers — first-principles, atomistic, coarse-grained, pore-scale, phenomenological, process-level — that do not connect, so that no chain of models runs from a synthesis recipe to a measured permeance. That specific structural gap, rather than the absence of cellulose studies in the machine-learning literature, is the argument for a data-driven approach. The representation–model–task framework is then executed task by task across property prediction, synthesis optimisation with Bayesian optimisation, inverse design, microstructural analysis and fouling forecasting, with four mandatory decisions — representation, model, task, validation — made explicit for each, and interpretability treated as a validation instrument whose attributions are falsifiable by synthesis. Cellulose/iron-oxide composites for oil–water separation serve as a running example throughout. Data resources are assessed for cellulose coverage rather than catalogued; methodological pitfalls are given cellulose-specific manifestations and mitigations; and under-explored niches are classified by operational criteria under a stated, repeatable search protocol.
items.authors: Ye O. Kolomiiets

items.title: Computational corroboration, at the sign level, that R-phenibut is the GABA-B eutomer: a two-sided alchemical transfer free-energy validation
items.abstract: Phenibut (β‑phenyl‑γ‑aminobutyric acid) is taken as a racemate, but its two enantiomers are not equivalent at its principal target, the GABA‑B receptor complex. This study asks one narrow question: which enantiomer is the eutomer at GABA‑B, and can a physics‑based relative binding free energy (RBFE) method answer it within a stated uncertainty? Calculations used the open‑source Alchemical Transfer Method (ATM) in AToM‑OpenMM at the orthosteric site of the 4MS4 Venus‑flytrap domain, on a 22‑state λ‑ladder with replica exchange and autocorrelation-corrected UWHAM estimation. The method was licensed on a two‑sided edge first: R‑phenibut → arbaclofen (H→Cl) returned ΔΔG = −1.890 ± 0.368 kcal/mol against a measured bracket of ≈ −1.6 to −2.0, correct in sign and inside the bracket. That edge is a substitution, not a stereoinversion, so no enantiomer edge here is validated two‑sided. Three independent seeds are reported as separate rows andarenot averaged: ΔΔG(R→S) =+1.673± 0.321,+0.633±0.302 and+0.783±0.304 kcal/mol. All three are positive, soR‑phenibut is theeutomer at GABA‑B. The claim is the sign, not the magnitude. The magnitude moves the other way. Seeds 2 and 3 agree to 0.150 kcal/mol while seed 1, the first completed, lies about 1 kcal/mol above both and is the one that does not replicate. The between‑seed scatter (SD 0.562) exceeds every individual corrected error, so single‑run bars understate the true uncertainty; two pre‑registered tests for a sampling defect in seed 1 both returned negative, so the spread is carried as genuine between‑run variance. Against the one‑sided experimental floor ΔΔG ≥ +1.42 kcal/mol, seeds 2, 3 and the three‑seed mean (+1.03) fall below, so the protocol under‑predicts the magnitude. With zero completed λ round trips these ± are statistical‑only lower bounds that exclude force‑field error, and the seeds share one force field, one protonation assignment and one receptor structure, so the sign rests most firmly on the experiment together with the validation edge. The same machinery fails at phenibut’s second target, α2δ‑1. The H→Cl edge is wrong‑signed (−0.805 ± 0.303 against experimental +1.13), and a gabapentin → pregabalin control lands at +12.846 ± 0.449 against an expected≈−0.21—a ~13 kcal/mol miss that passes every standard convergence gate. An initial attribution to a broken λ‑ladder splice did not survive a direct test of the saved trajectories and is withdrawn; the failure mechanism is unresolved. No α2δ‑1 number is biology, and no two‑target sign‑inversion claim is made. The contribution is the pairing: a licensed regime and a documented‑failure regime, each reported with its full uncertainty.
items.authors: Andrei Mihai Visalon

items.title: Self-recycling Fenton chemistry through the ordered hydration shells of Fe
items.abstract: The century-old Fenton reaction has been constrained by the kinetic bottleneck of Fe3+/Fe2+ cycling, which demands excessive iron dosing and generates hazardous sludge. Here we report that Fe3+ ions intrinsically bypass this limitation through a remote through-space ligand effect that induces long-range ordering of water molecules beyond the first coordination shell. This ordered hydration network functions as a visible-to-red-light antenna via a collective water-network-to-metal charge transfer mechanism, continuously generating electrons that reduce Fe3+ to Fe2+ without exogenous photocatalysts or chemical reductants. This self-sustaining cycle achieves approximately 80% TOC removal of phenol in a scaled-up 15 L reactor under natural sunlight and sustains approximately 65% TOC removal over 20 consecutive cycles for real pharmaceutical wastewater, with only 1.2% iron loss per cycle and near-zero sludge generation. This work transforms a canonical kinetic barrier into a self-regenerating catalytic platform, uncovering a hydration-driven photochemical route that offers sustainable, sludge-free, sunlight-driven water purification.
items.authors: Qi Zhang, Xuan Guo, Ruihan Wang, Hu Shi, Jie Wang, Jianghong Zhao

items.title: Mechanochemical Birch-type hydrodefluorination of polytetrafluoroethylene: amine-controlled hydrogenation versus carbonization
items.abstract: Reductive defluorination of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) can efficiently recover fluoride but commonly converts the carbon component into poorly defined carbonaceous solids. Herein, we report a mechanochemical Birch-type hydrodefluorination using lithium and ethylenediamine (EDA) that couples C-F bond cleavage with hydrogen incorporation. Milling at 30 Hz and room temperature released fluoride in 98% yield within 10 min, as independently determined by quantitative 19F NMR spectroscopy and ion chromatography. The pale-brown residue contained 0.6 wt% fluorine, 78.4 wt% carbon, and 12.3 wt% hydrogen, corresponding to an atomic H/C ratio of 1.88. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, solid-state 13C-MAS NMR, and powder X-ray diffraction showed loss of the PTFE C-F fingerprint and emergence of a CH2-rich structure with polyethylene-like thermal and crystalline features. The product is therefore assigned as a polyethylene-like material rather than chemically pure polyethylene. In the absence of EDA, fluoride was again obtained in 98% yield, whereas the solid product was a black, disordered sp2rich carbon. Coarser PTFE powders likewise tended to afford darker solids despite nearly quantitative fluoride recovery. These results demonstrate that fluoride yield alone is not a measure of hydrodefluorination selectivity and that EDA controls the competition between hydrogen incorporation and carbonization. The method converts PTFE into an inorganic fraction containing LiF and a hydrogen-rich carbon material potentially suitable for downstream polyolefin valorization.
items.authors: Masashi Hattori, Hibiki Ota, Moe Fujishiro, Kanako Inoo, Yosuke Kishikawa, Zhengyu Zhao

items.title: Switching from orthosteric to allosteric inhibition: Discovery of N-aryl-1H-azaindole-derived allosteric
items.abstract: The cytosolic protein tyrosine phosphatase SHP2 is an emerging therapeutic target due to its central role in oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase and immune checkpoint signaling. Although allosteric SHP2 inhibitors have entered clinical trials, they often lack efficacy as single agents and display reduced potency against activated SHP2 mutants. New allosteric SHP2 inhibitor chemotypes and a deeper understanding of allosteric SHP2 modulation are therefore needed. Herein, we report N -aryl-1 H -azaindazoles as a novel class of allosteric SHP2 inhibitors. A scaffold-hopping strategy led to the conversion of an orthosteric SHP2 inhibitor into an allosteric inhibitor. Structure-activity relationship studies, including a systematic investigation of the scaffold, led to the identification of compound 67 . Compound 67 inhibits SHP2 through an exclusively allosteric mechanism and shows potent activity across various cancer cell lines, including AML cells overexpressing the activated SHP2 E76K mutant. X-ray crystallography and computational analyses elucidated key molecular determinants underlying the steep structureactivity relationships of this inhibitor series, providing a structural basis for further optimization.
items.authors: Nina-Louisa Efrém, Machoud Amoussa, Yvette Roske, Feng Bo, Ziqiong Guo, Katrin Jana Frank

items.title: Emerging Paradigms in Electrochemical Water Treatment: Advanced Electrode Materials, Resource Recovery, and Machine Learning
items.abstract: Electrochemical water treatment offers a versatile approach to contaminant removal and resource recovery, although its practical performance depends on electrode properties, wastewater composition and operating conditions. This review critically examines the principal electrochemical treatment methods, including electrochemical oxidation and reduction, electro-Fenton processes, electrocoagulation, electroflotation, electrodeposition and electrodialysis. Their reaction pathways, treatment capabilities and limitations are discussed, with particular attention to the distinction between pollutant degradation, separation and recovery. Electrode development is examined through boron-doped diamond, mixed metal oxides and two-dimensional materials, including graphene derivatives, MXenes, transition-metal dichalcogenides and black phosphorus. The discussion considers how surface chemistry, electronic structure and electrode architecture influence charge transfer, reactive-species generation and ion transport, while addressing stability, material release and performance in complex wastewater matrices. Commercial implementation is assessed in relation to energy consumption, electrode lifetime, reactor design, maintenance requirements and integration with existing treatment infrastructure. The review also explores the application of machine learning to predict treatment performance, identify influential operating variables and guide material selection and process optimization. Particular emphasis is placed on data quality, model interpretability and validation beyond laboratory datasets. By connecting treatment mechanisms, electrode engineering and data-driven optimization, this review identifies the evidence and development priorities needed to advance electrochemical technologies towards reliable, economically viable water treatment.
items.authors: Srikanth Ponnada, Anuradha Ponnada, Abhilasha Bhawsar, Subash Chandra Bose Rapaka, Rakesh K Sharma

items.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Carbazole-Thioisatin Spirocycles via NHC-Catalyzed Remote N–H Activation
items.abstract: An enantioselective NHC-catalyzed strategy for the synthesis of spirocyclic carbazole derivatives was developed through oxidative remote N–H activation of readily available 1-formylcarbazoles. Catalytic generation of aza-ortho-quinone methides enables efficient annulation with thioisatins, underexplored electrophiles in asymmetric NHC catalysis. The protocol is also compatible with conventional isatins, affording structurally diverse spirocyclic heteroaromatic products in acceptable to good yields (up to 76%) and enantiomeric ratios up to 98:2 er. The utility of the method was demonstrated on gram-scale, while successful coupling with an acyclic ketone further illustrates the broader synthetic potential of this remote N–H activation process.
items.authors: Ladislav Lóška, Ivana Císařová, Jan Veselý

items.title: Room-temperature relithiation of chemically delithiated LMFP cathode materials as a model for direct recycling
items.abstract: Room-temperature direct relithiation is an attractive strategy for the regeneration of olivine-type cathode materials, but its applicability to LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 (LMFP) remains largely unexplored. Here, chemically delithiated LMFP powders were used as model materials to evaluate the feasibility and limitations of direct regeneration under mild conditions. Different delithiation levels were obtained using Ferric nitrate or Nitronium tetrafluoroborate as oxidizing agents, enabling selective oxidation of Fe 2+ or combined oxidation of Fe 2+ and Mn 2+ depending on the oxidizing strength. The structural and redox evolution from pristine to delithiated and relithiated states was followed by X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, Mössbauer spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and electrochemical testing. Relithiation was carried out at room temperature using lithium iodide in organic media, including acetonitrile and ethanol. The results show that LMFP can be efficiently relithiated when lithium loss is mainly associated with Fe 2+ oxidation, with substantial recovery of the olivine structure and electrochemical activity. However, higher delithiation levels involving Mn oxidation lead to incomplete regeneration, likely due to manganese dissolution and irreversible local structural changes. These findings demonstrate that LMFP cannot be considered as a simple extension of LFP in direct recycling processes. Instead, manganese-containing olivine cathodes require specific regeneration strategies adapted to their redox chemistry and degradation pathways. Studies on real end-of-life LMFP electrodes will be required to validate the conclusions obtained from these model materials.
items.authors: Duresa K. Usula, Tassadit Ouaneche, Lorenzo Stievano, Laure Monconduit, Nadir Recham, Moulay Tahar Sougrati

items.title: Direct Synthesis of Ag-In-Zn-S Quantum Dot Inks for Solution-Processed Optoelectronics
items.abstract: Non-toxic I–III–VI quantum dots (QDs) hold strong potential for optoelectronics but are hindered by complex synthesis and post-processing requirements. Here, we demonstrate a direct synthesis of Zn-alloyed AgIn 5 S 8 (AIZS) QDs that produces high-quality inks in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF). The colloidal stability originates from a synergistic solvation layer comprising surface-bound oxygen-coordinated In/Zn–DMF complexes, co-adsorbed butylamine, and residual iodide anions. The resulting QDs exhibit strong n-type character and photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of ca. 43%. Proof-of-concept Quantum Dot Ligh emitting Diodes (QDLEDs) were fabricated based on this material, demonstrating the feasibility of processing functional emitting layers directly from polar inks.
items.authors: Apostolos Kalafatis, Spyros Orfanoudakis, Kostas Karaslanidis, Polychronis Tsipas, Alexandros Banis, Thomas Stergiopoulos

items.title: Orthogonal-Solvent Sequential Depositionfor Chiral Induction in Polymer Films andCircularly Polarized Light-Emitting Diodes
items.abstract: Solution-processed chiroptical polymer films are commonly prepared by blending a fluorescent polymer with a chiral inducer, which restricts material selection to components soluble in a common formulation solvent. Here we decouple the two solvent requirements by sequentially depositing poly(9,9-dioctylfluorene-alt-bithiophene) (F8T2) from chlorobenzene and a chiral inducer from ethanol, followed by thermal annealing. With (R)-(−)-1,1′-binaphthyl-2,2′-diyl hydrogen phosphate (R-DbHP), the sequential film reaches a peak apparent absorption dissymmetry factor of 0.35, compared with 0.09 for the best tetrahydrofuran-blend film under separately optimized conditions. The chiroptical response develops during annealing and is largely retained after ethanol treatment reduces the characteristic absorbance of the inducer overlayer. The strategy transfers to a second inducer, R-5011, and the resulting emissive layers operate in circularly polarized light-emitting diodes (CP-LEDs), giving electroluminescence dissymmetry factors of 0.79–0.83 at the emission maximum across four devices. The largest CD-derived values are designated apparent because their raw ellipticities exceed the nominal full-scale range; front/back measurements and an in-range concentration series characterize the signal while not excluding all polarization artifacts. Orthogonal-solvent sequential deposition thus provides a processing route to chiroptical polymer films and CP-LEDs without requiring the polymer and inducer to share a casting solvent.
items.authors: Hsin-Tso Chen

items.title: Q-Chem/CP2K software interface for projection-based, pseudoperiodic wavefunction-in-DFT embedding
items.abstract: We report an implementation of projection-based quantum embedding that combines periodic density functional theory in the CP2K code with correlated wavefunction calculations in the Q-Chem program. Using this interface, correlated wavefunction methods can be applied to a subset of the molecular orbitals, selected in an automated manner based on a user-defined list of nuclei, wth an embedding potential that provides electronic coupling to the remaining orbitals that comprise the environment. Our implementation uses exact projection, without the need for any level-shift operator, and is “pseudoperiodic” in the sense that periodic boundary effects are implicit in the orbitals used in the (non-periodic) wavefunction calculation. Convergence tests demonstrate that computed properties are faithful to the corresponding periodic quantities, provided that the high-level subsystem is spatially localized and small, relative to the periodic simulation cell. Spectroscopic examples for aqueous chromophores demonstrate converged results using a very limited subset of the water molecules in the simulation cell, decoupling the choice of excited-state method and basis set from the functional that is used to propagate ground-state ab initio molecular dynamics. Solvatochromic shifts for aqueous uracil are converged using equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory, without the need for solvent molecules in the wavefunction calculation, and the embedded calculation captures solvent effects that are absent in gas-phase “microhydration” studies.
items.authors: Ar. M. Fonlon, Elena Kolodzeiski, Dustin R. Broderick, Kay Carter-Fenk, Christopher J. Mundy, Christopher J. Stein

items.title: Domino and Cascade Reactions in Sustainable Synthesis: Activation Modes, Assessment Boundaries, and the Molecular-Process Discrepancy
items.abstract: Domino and cascade reactions construct molecular complexity through sequential transformations and can reduce intermediate isolation. Their contribution to sustainable synthesis depends on whether these advantages persist when precursor preparation, catalyst production, reaction operation, and product recovery are included. This targeted narrative review examines thirteen mechanistic examples across seven activation or propagation modes and develops the molecular-process discrepancy (MPD) as a framework for testing that translation. MPD connects a specific reaction-level claim to the additional material and energy requirements introduced by expanding the assessment boundary. It complements atom economy, process mass intensity, E-factor, life-cycle assessment, and process benchmarks without replacing their measurements. Four case studies distinguish the roles of feedstock and product recovery in Ambrox synthesis, oxidant substitution in coumestan formation, advanced-substrate preparation in lasalocid A biosynthesis, and operational consolidation in oseltamivir synthesis. Together, they show why atom conservation, selective ring construction, and fewer isolations provide different forms of efficiency that must be evaluated separately. The analysis identifies precursor access, dilution, separation, catalyst lifetime, and heat, light, or oxygen delivery as specific targets for process improvement. MPD provides a procedure for determining whether a proposed cascade advantage is retained, attenuated, reversed, or unresolved across explicit assessment boundaries.
items.authors: Khang T. Hoa

items.title: Reversing Benzene Bioisosterism through Photocatalytically Divergent Double Strain-Release Skeletal Remodeling
items.abstract: Highly functionalized two-dimensional molecular frameworks are vital in drug discovery, but their regioselective synthesis remains challenging. Here, we present a photocatalytic method that reverses the conventional paradigm of replacing planar aromatic rings with three-dimensional C(sp3)-rich bioisosteres. Instead, this technique converts bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) back into highly functionalized benzenes. This process creates a reversible link between three-dimensional and planar chemical spaces via divergent double-strain-release steps. By tuning the photocatalyst to favor either energy transfer or electron transfer pathways, distinct regioselective skeletal rearrangements were achieved from common BCB precursors. The method works with many functional groups and substitution patterns, enabling direct synthesis of densely functionalized benzenes that are otherwise difficult to produce regioselectively. Combined experimental and computational data revealed the reaction mechanisms in which photoinduced energy or electron transfer produces intermediates that undergo strain release and radical rearrangement in sequence. These results demonstrate strain-release skeletal remodeling as a way to switch between three-dimensional and planar chemical spaces, providing a complementary strategy to traditional benzene bioisosterism.
items.authors: Braja Kishor Paul, Malekul Islam, Pintu Kumbhakar, Pooja Bhardwaj, Fadil Faizal Mannighayil, Zheng-Wang Qu

items.title: Microstructural Evolution of Coffee Beans during Aqueous-based Decaffeination
items.abstract: Aqueous decaffeination removes caffeine before roasting but may also alter the green-bean microstructure that contributes to subsequent heat and mass transfer. This study used X-ray micro-computed tomography (µ-CT) to quantify time-dependent changes in the three-dimensional pore structure of intact Colombian Arabica coffee beans treated using a laboratory-scale protocol termed the Thame Water Method (TWM). Two beans were imaged in their raw states. One was subsequently imaged after 8 hr of treatment, while the second was imaged after 5 min and 30 min of treatment. Pore number decreased in both treatment windows, falling by approximately 22% after 30 min and 68% after 8 hr. During 30 min short-duration treatment, mean pore diameter and resolved porosity increased, whereas both decreased following prolonged treatment of 8 hr. A numerical model informed by the measured microstructures predicted slower heating for the 30 min microstructure and faster heating for the 8 hr microstructure relative to the raw bean under the same roasting profile. These findings show that aqueous decaffeination can alter the physical starting structure of green coffee beans and suggest that these changes may influence subsequent heating transfer during roasting. The TWM provides a µ-CT-compatible platform and a methodology to investigate structural changes produced by other decaffeination processes. A more complete understanding could ultimately support decisions about how decaffeinated coffee is processed and roasted for optimal cup quality.
items.authors: Robert Scott Young, Liam Micheal Farrell, Lorna Sinclair, Danielle Duggins, Sara Nonni, Andrew R. T. Morrison

items.title: Atomistic Probability Kinetic Modeling of Polymer Functionalization: A Framework for Post-Functionalization and Upcycling of Polymers
items.abstract: Post-functionalization and the upcycling of post-consumer waste are valuable strategies for enhancing the material properties and value of polymers, but predictive modeling of these reactions is limited because of their inherent randomness. We present a mathematical framework to describe the effect of polymer functionalization reactions on downstream material properties or products using a combinatoric atomistic probability distribution (APD). The APD is derived generally to predict the spacing of subchains, Δ, between substituents or at chain ends when S substituents are randomly distributed along a polymer chain of length L. This approach is applied to a model upcycling system: the functionalization of polyethylene (PE) via sulfonation and subsequent H 2 O 2 -driven oxidative depolymerization. By coupling the APD with models for downstream depolymerization of sulfonated PE and hydroxyl radical-mediated decomposition kinetics, we develop a kinetic probability distribution (KPD) that explicitly describes the resulting degradation products. This approach results in dimensional reduction by requiring 14 total parameters for an N-species system (N = 6 here), while traditional modeling approaches require 4N + 7 (31 in our case). Probability parameters obtained from the KPD enabled the calculation of product and CO 2 carbon yields within ~10% of experimental values. This framework presents a novel approach to incorporating the underlying randomness governing polymer functionalization reactions, vastly reducing the parameter space and improving targeting of more economically relevant products during upcycling.
items.authors: Brandon D. Howard, Christian J. Howard, Aspen Tapley, John R. Dorgan, Scott Calabrese Barton

items.title: Concise Total Synthesis of (–)-5-epi-Cycloclavine via Metal- and Base-Free Diastereoselective Intramolecular Cyclopropanation of N-Sulfonylhydrazone-Derived Donor Carbene
items.abstract: A metal- and base-free intramolecular cyclopropanation based on nonstabilized donor carbenes generated in situ from N-sulfonylhydrazones has been developed, enabling the construction of the highly strained aza[3.1.0]bicyclic core of (–)-5-epi-cycloclavine with concomitant complete stereocontrol of two all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. Combined with the straightforward introduction of methacrylic acid as four-carbon fragment from readily available enantiopure functionalized tricyclic indole derivative (4-amino Uhle's ketone), this strategy enabled a concise diasteroselective synthesis of the five-fused rings system present in (–)-5-epi-cycloclavine.
items.authors: Francesca Diotallevi, Francesca Bartoccini, Giovanni Piersanti

items.title: Mature complexes carry more G protein class information than partner free GPCR structures
items.abstract: GPCR structures are widely used to infer G protein coupling and pathway selective pharmacology, but mature receptor G protein complexes may contain structural information acquired or stabilized after partner selection. We asked how much G protein class information is present independently of the bound transducer. We analyzed 1,360 experimental class A GPCR structures using structural bioinformatics, molecular recognition descriptors and receptor grouped machine learning. Every receptor with both a strict partner free active structure and a G protein bound structure entered the matched analysis; activation and evolutionary transfer served as controls. Twelve receptors met the strict criteria. Bound endpoints gave a larger G protein class margin in 11 of 12 receptors (mean difference 0.389, 95% CI 0.095 to 0.682; exact sign flip P = 0.030), with macro ROC AUC 0.795 versus 0.619. A four feature geometry classified activation at ROC AUC 0.996 across 1,336 structures from 199 receptors. Across 207 receptor transducer units, class information was distributed across sequence and structural properties, strongly shaped by evolutionary relatedness, and no universal cross family interface rule emerged. Mature GPCR complexes therefore contain receptor compatibility plus information associated with the selected and stabilized transducer. Similarity to a G protein bound endpoint supports compatibility with that signalling state but does not by itself establish intrinsic coupling preference, a distinction relevant to pathway selective drug discovery.
items.authors: Hossein Batebi

items.title: Cationic Conductive Aluminum Metal-Organic Framework Couples Ion Exchange and Redox Chemistry for Oxyanion Detoxification
items.abstract: We report Al-HOTP, [Al 3 (HOTP) 2 (H 2 O) 6 ][Al 3 (HOTP)(H 2 O) 12 ] (SO 4 ) 2 (HOTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaoxytriphenylene), a cationic two-dimensional electrically conductive metal-organic framework (MOF) that couples counterion-exchange chemistry with a redox-active framework for oxyanion capture and detoxification. While triphenylene-based honeycomb conductive frameworks are well established, the Al-based analog reported here is, to the best of our knowledge, the first of its kind, and demonstrates how cationic ion-exchange chemistry can be combined with framework-mediated redox activity for multifunctional water remediation. Al-HOTP efficiently removes permanganate (MnO 4 − ) and dichromate (Cr 2 O 7 2− ) from water while promoting their conversion to lower-valent, less toxic Mn(IV)- and Cr(III)-containing species. The framework removes approximately 95% of MnO 4 − and 90% of Cr 2 O 7 2− from 30 ppm solutions within 5 min and exhibits an experimentally demonstrated uptake capacity of up to 1600 mg g −1 for MnO 4 − and 300 mg g −1 for Cr 2 O 7 2− . To the best of our knowledge, the MnO 4 − adsorption capacity is the highest reported for a MOF-based permanganate adsorbent. Mechanistic studies support a cooperative capture-and-reduction mechanism in which sulfate-to-oxyanion exchange promotes initial uptake, followed by electron transfer from the redox-active HOTP ligands to the captured oxyanions. The resulting framework oxidation increases the demand for charge-compensating anions, enabling additional uptake beyond the initial sulfate-exchange capacity. Beyond batch uptake, Al-HOTP maintains efficient contaminant removal over 36 consecutive filtration passes and can be integrated into an FTO-based electrode for proof-of-concept electrochemical detection of both oxyanions. Overall, this work establishes the coupling of permanent cationic character with framework redox activity as a design strategy for integrating high-capacity capture, reductive detoxification, regeneration, and device functionality for multifunctional water remediation.
items.authors: Satya P. Suman, Christian Sandoval-Pauker, M. R. Dontireddy, Ahad H. Javed, Zina Deriche, Moneer Alenezi

items.title: Resolving Positional Markush Structures for Chemical Reaction Extraction
items.abstract: The automated extraction of chemical reaction data from scientific literature remains very challenging mainly due to the visual complexity and heterogeneity of published graphical schemes. In particular, substrate scopes containing positional Markush structures pose a significant challenge for current Optical Chemical Structure Recognition (OCSR) and reaction-extraction systems, as their resolution requires combining molecular recognition with precise spatial reasoning. Herein, we introduce a deterministic, coordinate-based extraction pipeline designed to resolve positional Markush structures in reaction schemes. Building upon a fine-tuned version of the graph-prediction OCSR module MolScribe, our approach uses deterministic geometric rules based on 2D molecular coordinates to infer R-group attachment points and generate topologically valid molecular representations. To evaluate this approach, we introduce two curated benchmarks: MIPub-2k (Molecular Images from Publication - Université Bourgogne Europe) comprising 2,128 literature-derived molecular image crops for OCSR evaluation and MIReactPub (Markush template-based Image of Reaction from Publication – Université Bourgogne Europe) comprising 450 reactions from 23 schemes containing positional Markush structures for reaction-level assessment. The complete pipeline achieves an end-to-end F1 score of 0.46, increasing to 0.54 for schemes without textual-dependent ambiguities. Slightly reorganizing figures doubles the F1 score, demonstrating the robustness of the underlying geometric resolution while highlighting the substantial impact of visual heterogeneity in published literature on end-to-end performance. By explicitly encoding chemical and spatial constraints, our proposed approach provides a transparent and reproducible framework for resolving complex molecular representations from literature images. The resulting open-source pipeline and benchmarks provide a specialized component that can be further integrated into automated workflows for large-scale chemical information extraction.
items.authors: Ulrick Fineddie Randriharimanamizara, Atif Anwer, Julien Roger, Fabrice Meriaudeau, Paul Fleurat-Lessard

items.title: Manufacturing process modeling of bilayer cathode for graded thick electrode design
items.abstract: The energy density and rate capability of lithium-ion batteries can be improved through the design of bilayer and compositionally graded architectures for thick electrodes. For this, manufacturing steps such as drying and calendering are key considerations, since they determine the final electrode microstructure and therefore affect its electrochemical performance. Here, we extend our previously developed processcoupled coarse-grained molecular dynamics and discrete element method manufacturing computational workflow from single-layer LiNi0.33Co0.33Mn0.33O2 cathodes to bilayer cathode architectures. The model accounts for active material particles with realistic shapes obtained from X-ray micro-computed tomography. We use bilayer cathodes with different layer formulations as study cases. The Our simulation results show that the initial through-thickness heterogeneity can be preserved after slurry drying but is progressively reshaped during calendering. The layer-averaged porosity contrast can be weakened or even reversed under compression. This indicates a transition from porosity heterogeneity arising from slurry drying to residual porosity governed more by formulation-dependent particle packing. Meanwhile, the interfacial mixing region between the two layers broadens and the effective tortuosity factor increases sharply in the low-porosity regime. These results demonstrate that bilayer electrode design should be treated as a process-history-dependent engineering problem rather than as a static layer stacking one.
items.authors: Lei Qin, Francisco Fernandez, Rares-George Scurtu, Margret Wohlfahrt-Mehrens, Alejandro A. Franco

items.title: Direct Ink Writing (DIW) of Mechanically Graded and Programmable Crosslinked Polymers with Seamless Interlayer Fusion
items.abstract: Direct ink writing (DIW) enables the fabrication of complex polymer architectures under mild processing conditions, yet the production of mechanically graded multimaterial structures remains limited by weak interfacial adhesion and by the restricted availability of printable thermoset feedstocks. Here, we introduce a high internal phase emulsion (HIPE)-based printing platform for the fabrication of mechanically programmable crosslinked polymers with seamless interlayer integration. Oil-in-water HIPE inks were formulated from methacrylated dextran (DexMA) in the continuous phase and mixtures of methyl methacrylate and hexyl methacrylate in the dispersed phase, yielding printable precursors that generate crosslinked networks spanning elastic moduli from below 1 MPa to above 150 MPa after curing. Rheological and morphological analyses demonstrated that the different formulations possess comparable printability despite their markedly different final mechanical properties. Photo-rheological experiments revealed a two-stage curing process, consisting of rapid DexMA crosslinking followed by slower polymerization of the monomer-rich phase, providing a temporal window that promotes molecular interpenetration across adjacent deposited filaments. This mechanism enables the formation of intermolecularly fused interfaces rather than conventional layer-by-layer contacts. Monomaterial and multimaterial constructs were fabricated and mechanically characterized under compression. While multimaterial architectures exhibited compressive moduli comparable to intermediate-composition controls, they displayed substantially enhanced toughness and enabled programmable deformation and recovery behaviors. The ability to sequentially combine mechanically distinct formulations within a continuous crosslinked network, while maintaining robust interlayer cohesion, establishes HIPE-based DIW as a versatile strategy for the fabrication of mechanically graded thermoset architectures whose performance emerges from the interplay between material composition and spatial design.
items.authors: F. Serpe, L. Scozzafava, R. Angelini, A. Martinelli, M.C. Tirelli, M. Costantini

items.title: Nanodiscs can preferentially enrich transmembrane proteins in a bottom-up proteomic analysis workflow
items.abstract: Membrane proteins are critically important pharmaceutical targets and thus their analytical characterization is vital to drug development efforts. However, compared to cytosolic proteins, membrane proteins are generally more difficult to purify and/or analytically characterize in part due to their amphipathic nature. Nanodiscs (NDs) have become a popular membrane mimetic system offering a well-defined lipid bilayer environment to stabilize membrane proteins for in vitro analyses. NDs based on membrane scaffold proteins (MSPs) offer advantages in terms of their amenability to purification and control over lipid composition. Here we investigated the utility of MSP NDs having different diameters and lipid compositions to enrich membrane proteins isolated from cells for bottom-up proteomic characterization. Specifically, we coupled a robust ND formation and purification workflow with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis to determine the identity and relative abundance of proteins incorporated into NDs made using different synthesis conditions. We found that the ND diameter had an effect on the relative enrichment of detected proteins and protein classes; however, lipid composition did not have a significant effect. The data indicated that this ND-based approach selectively allowed for the detection of membrane proteins and membrane associated proteins over cytosolic protein contaminants. Furthermore, we found that transmembrane proteins, which are particularly hard to extract and analyze using traditional membrane mimetics, were significantly enriched when using NDs compared to detergent micelles. These results suggest that MSP ND-based approaches could be applied to the selective enrichment of membrane proteins from cells in a manner that could be enabling for both proteomic and other analytical characterization approaches.
items.authors: Hanyu Zheng, Marina C. Sarcinella, Brandon T. Ruotolo, Ryan C. Bailey

items.title: Classical infrared correlation rules as diagnostic tests: likelihood ratios from 6,663 experimental spectra
items.abstract: Infrared correlation tables give, for each functional group, a wavenumber window and an adjective. They do not say how often a band is found in that window when the group is absent, and that is the number that decides whether the observation is evidence. We treated every published rule as a diagnostic test. A set of 101 rules for 60 functional groups, transcribed from one widely used interpretation course and frozen before any confirmatory analysis, was scored on 1,539 ATR spectra of synthesised compounds from the Chemotion repository and replicated on 5,124 transmission spectra from the NIST Chemistry WebBook, with the deposited structure as ground truth and sensitivity, specificity and likelihood ratios as the metrics. The main result is a division of the spectrum into two regimes. Above 1500 cm−1 most rules carry real evidence (median positive likelihood ratio 2.8 and 3.0 in the two collections, up to 43 for the saturated ester carbonyl); in the fingerprint region, at or below 1350 cm−1, band position alone is close to uninformative (median 1.1 and 1.2), because almost every spectrum has a band in almost every window. The rankings agree across the two collections (Spearman 0.79; 87% of rules within a factor of two). The audit also measures what the tables leave unsaid: intensity qualifiers cost more sensitivity than they buy specificity (the nitrile band reaches the stated intensity in one nitrile in ten), the benzene substitution patterns do not reach a likelihood ratio of 5 in either collection, and several rules are far more useful for ruling a group out than for ruling it in. We provide the quantified table, the frozen rule set and the scripts so that the audit can be extended to further rules and collections.
items.authors: Kementsu Ibarguen Calvo

items.title: Water hydrogen bond network elongation below the lower critical solution temperature in aqueous triethylamine solution probed by soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy
items.abstract: The lower critical solution temperature (LCST) mechanism of aqueous triethylamine (TEA) solution was investigated by the element-specific observation of molecular interactions using soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS). The H 2 O‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds were probed by O K-edge XAS, and the hydrophobic interactions of TEA and TEA‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds were probed by C and N K-edge XAS. Molecular interactions in aqueous TEA solutions at temperatures below the LCST were analyzed using radial distribution functions obtained from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Temperature-dependent changes in the XAS spectra were evaluated by inner-shell calculations using snapshots from MD simulations. These studies revealed that the LCST mechanism of aqueous TEA solution is governed by the balance of H 2 O‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions of TEA, and TEA‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds. Aqueous TEA solution is miscible below the LCST, where the H 2 O‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds elongate owing to the TEA‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions of TEA. The H 2 O‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds near the LCST are closer to those of liquid water owing to the weakening of the TEA‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds. The hydrophobic interactions of TEA are also enhanced owing to the strong H 2 O‒H 2 O hydrogen bonds, resulting in liquid‒liquid phase separation above the LCST. These three factors provide a framework for interpreting the LCST mechanisms of amphiphilic molecules, polymers, and soft matter related to protein folding and DNA packing.
items.authors: Masanari Nagasaka, Kenji Mochizuki

items.title: Chiral Doping of Two-Dimensional Molecular Crystals for Circularly Polarized Photodetection
items.abstract: 2 Abstract Circularly polarized (CP) photodetection is essential for applications such as quantum communication, biomedical imaging, and secure optical encryption. Direct CP photodetection using chiral organic materials has attracted growing interest owing to their structural tunability and solution processability; however, it requires both strong chiroptical response and efficient charge transport. Two-dimensional molecular crystals (2DMCs) are attractive photoactive systems with ordered molecular packing and favorable charge transport, but lack intrinsic chirality. Here, we develop a chiral doping strategy to introduce chiroptical activity into 2DMCs for efficient CP photodetection. An achiral diphenyl-substituted boron–nitrogen-embedded anthracene derivative bearing hexyl side chains is designed as the host, while chiral molecules with the same conjugated backbone and chiral side chains serve as dopants. The resulting doped films combine chiroptical response with ordered molecular packing. The corresponding phototransistor devices exhibit favorable charge transport and ultraviolet CP photodetection performance, with a maximum mobility of 0.45 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , a maximum responsivity of 8.2×10 2 A W −1 , and an average photocurrent dissymmetry factor of 0.17, representing competitive performance among reported direct organic CP phototransistors. Furthermore, CPlight-based information encoding and decoding are demonstrated. This strategy endows 2DMCs with chiroptical activity, providing a platform for CP photodetection and chiral optoelectronic applications.
items.authors: Lijuan Zhang, Cheng-Zhuo Du, Yu-Zeng Gao, Wanhui Li, Hao-Han Lv, Haonan Sun

items.title: Uni-Macro-FRPN: Full-Resolution and Cross-Scale Learning for Polymers
items.abstract: Polymer properties emerge from interactions across scales, yet existing polymer models typically preserve either detailed monomer chemistry without an explicit polymer graph or polymer connectivity with simplified monomer representations, due to computational constraints, as polymers typically contain tens of thousands of atoms. We present Uni-Macro-FRPN (FRPN), a Full-Resolution Polymer Network that retains both detailed atom-level and monomer-level features and explicit polymer structure information within a unified framework. Two Transformers jointly learn atom-informed monomer semantics, sequence order, and chain topology from BigSMILES-derived representations. On the Block Copolymer Database (BCDB) lamellar-versus-non-lamellar classification task, FRPN achieves 86.4% accuracy and 90.6% ROC–AUC, establishing state-of-the-art performance. Ablation results indicate that the gain is not explained solely by increased parameter count. On a linear homopolymer benchmark, monomer-centric learning remains competitive, highlighting a boundary case where polymer-scale organization is simple. To test generalization beyond linear polymers, we further construct an all-atom molecular-dynamics benchmark of 1640 datapoints spanning diverse monomer chemistries, sequence orderings, chain topologies, and physical properties. FRPN achieves the strongest overall performance on this topology-rich benchmark, with diagnostics supporting the benefit of jointly modeling monomer chemistry and polymer structure. Taken together, FRPN provides a practical route for moving polymer representation learning beyond monomer-centric representations.
